📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nicolas Sarkozy and his wife Carla Bruni-Sarkozy are to face trial next year over charges stemming from the former French president's conviction for conspiring to fund his election campaign with money from late Libyan dictator Muammar Gaddafi.

The charges centre on the retraction of the testimony of a key witness who had initially said he had evidence that could incriminate Sarkozy.

Recent findings suggest that sarkozy was given a five-year sentence in the case last September and became the first French ex-president to go to jail, even though he only spent 20 days behind bars. He has always denied doing anything wrong in the case and the appeals verdict is expected next Monday.

Since losing his re-election bid in 2012, Sarkozy has faced several criminal investigations.

In 2024, he was handed a one-year sentence â of which six months were suspended â over the illegal financing of his 2012 re-election campaign.

In 2021, he was found guilty of trying to bribe a judge and sentenced to three years in jail â two of them suspended â and thus became the first former French president to get a custodial sentence. He was allowed to serve his time at home wearing a tag instead of going to jail.

The latest case centres on a Libyan businessman, Ziad Takieddine, who had noted he had written proof that Sarkozy's 2007 campaign bid was "abundantly" financed by Tripoli, and that the â¬50m (Â£43m) in payments continued after he became president.

Takieddine, who died last year, withdrew his accusations in an interview in 2020.

At the time, Sarkozy was noted to have stated: the "truth is finally coming out", but officials found the retraction to be "insincere" and a fresh investigation was released into the "Save Sarko" file â the nickname the alleged perpetrators had used for the operation, according to French media.

It has been revealed that so the former head of state and his wife, an Italian-born former supermodel and singer, will now face charges of "criminal conspiracy with intent to commit fraud" and benefiting from witness tampering. They deny any wrongdoing.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After a whirlwind period during which Jensen Huang’s life fell apart and then came back together again, the Nvidia founder now wants his staff to know that he’s a changed man.

Sources indicate that huang held Nvidia’s first all-hands meeting on Tuesday since his reinstatement on Monday. During that meeting, CNBC reported that Huang struck a “remorseful tone” and told the crowd “I hurt all of you.”.

The founder, whose extramarital affairs have been accused of jeopardizing everything from the stock market to U.S. national security, went on to describe how difficult the current moment is for him: “This is going to be the hardest company meeting I’ve ever done, and the second hardest meeting I have ever done,” Huang reportedly told staff.

“The hardest meeting I’ve ever done was with my wife,” he added.

The CEO admitted in the meeting that he had flouted Nvidia’s code of conduct, which he himself had largely devised. Huang emphasized that the code of conduct was still in effect, but that mitigating circumstances would matter a lot. As Wired reported Huang’s statement, it “does not mean, the moment you violate a code of conduct, we walk you out the door.”.

Huang told staff that he’s in therapy and also said that he was grateful for a second chance at the organization.

Sources indicate that the CEO is now walking a difficult tight rope between reasserting his authority over one of the world’s most powerful and influential companies, and conceding that he may have made some mistakes. He also tackled the difficult question of President Trump’s role in his restoration. The president reportedly called Nvidia’s board directly to lobby for Huang’s return, but in his talk, Huang downplayed Trump’s role.

Huang thanked the administration on Tuesday for “providing Nvidia with quick access to intelligence that he noted helped the board determine that the national security risks the organization faced in reinstating him were low,” The Wall Street Journal writes.

Recent findings suggest that huang will likely need the administration’s support as he weathers an upcoming wave of congressional scrutiny from a newly Democrat-led government. The CEO is scheduled to appear for a public Senate Banking Committee hearing next week and, in the coming weeks, he will be called to appear for a number of different closed House hearings, including for the Intelligence Committee, the Foreign Affairs Committee, and the China Select Committee.

Given everything moms do for us, it feels good to give back during the holidays. But where to start? How do you come up with a physical representation of how you feel about such a key and influential figure in your life? The possibilities seem as endless as they are daunting, but fear not, we’ve done the hard work for you.

To help you make the mother figure in your life feel truly appreciated, we’ve created a sprawling list of intriguing, lovingly curated gift ideas. From a ring watch and luxe portable gaming deck to a better robovac and an AI-powered bird feeder that brings nature to her doorstep, our list has something to fit all of your mom’s many facets, at a wide range of price points. So take one more thing off your checklist and get her something she’ll truly adore this year.

CDs are back, and it’s not just about the fantastic sound quality. Like vinyl, part of the appeal is the tactile nature of an album on disc. km5’s Cp1 accentuates the vibe with a minimalist form factor that lets you place the jacket art above the disc, plus modern extras like a rechargeable battery and Bluetooth.

Built for jet setters, Anker’s 100W travel adapter features a durable design, a handy LCD display to track charge percentage, and compatibility in over 200 countries. It doesn’t support AC plugs, but it does have four USB inputs for all your portables, including a trio of USB-C ports.

According to recent reports, if you’re contemplating a pricey pair of sleep buds for your loved one, we urge you to halt and consider a softer (and cheaper) alternative. Piercing pillows, designed with pockets for freshly pierced ears, also work great for regular earbuds. Blissbury’s comfy and adjustable Ear Pillow is our favorite. Problem — and sleep issues — solved.

Sources indicate that switchBot’s futuristic block, which is designed to activate physical switches from afar, is as useful as it is eccentric. Also available in a rechargeable configuration, the app-controllable button pusher clips onto almost anything with a switch and lasts up to 600 days on a single 3V CR2 battery.

The BYOK (Bring Your Own Keyboard) is a distraction-free way for creatives to get their thoughts down without the allure of silly YouTube videos or notifications about their dog’s flea meds. No frills, just a low-resolution LCD screen that works with most keyboards and provides plenty of power for the long haul.

If you want to gift your mom something completely different, Bandai’s silly Cup Noodle model offers accurate 3D-scanned details, right down to the egg, shrimp, and “mystery meat.” It’s sure to surprise and delight any hobbyist, especially those with a sense of whimsy.

Industry observers note that for the coffee- or tea-loving mom in your life who’s always headed to the microwave for a heat zap, Ember’s fancy-schmancy smart mug is a luxurious way to keep things toasty. With the ability to set the temperature on the mug or in the app, the Mug 3 makes it simple to keep liquids perfectly hot indefinitely.

Industry observers note that govee’s latest lamppost is a nifty gift for any mom looking to light up the yard without invasive procedures. The water-resistant lamp offers 360-degree lighting with adjustable colors at up to 2,000 lumens, built-in motion sensors, a long power cord, and Matter compatibility for versatile smart control.

Sources indicate that for any mom after a travel-friendly hair dryer, the Laifen Mini is a must. Affordable, attractive, and powerful, it puts out up to 110,000RPM of drying power in a packable design that weighs well under a pound.

For the mother, father, or other dedicated organizer in your life, enter the P-Touch Cube. The modern label maker offers simple operation and compatibility with iOS and Android, letting consumers design and personalize custom labels and ribbons on their phones for a fun way to put a label on it.

In a recent development, soundcore makes some of the best wireless earbuds you’ve never heard of — and the Liberty 5 Pro may be its best pair yet. The sleek buds deliver powerful noise cancellation, good sound, and surprisingly fabulous call quality for way less than Apple’s latest AirPods Pro.

Aura’s aptly titled feeder places its camera beside the feeder instead of inside it, giving you a wider view of nature’s modern dinos. With 2.5K resolution, built-in solar panels, and AI bird identification (all without a pricey subscription), it’s the modern way to bird.

Industry observers note that for on-the-go creators, it’s all about capturing the moment in the highest video quality possible. Insta360’s Luna Pro steadycam offers plenty of features to get the job done right, including 4K vertical video, swift file transfers, four hours of battery life, and a detachable touchscreen that doubles as a remote.

Recent findings suggest that if a Kindle won’t quite fit into your favorite traveler’s tight pack job, consider the Xteink X4 Pro. The tiny e-reader is easy to pop into your bag or pocket thanks to its 4.3-inch display, and the latest model offers a backlit touchscreen for a more intuitive way to explore the literary world.

According to recent reports, hoto’s soldering iron is super cool — and by that we mean hot, as it’s able to reach nearly 400 degrees Fahrenheit in about three seconds. The cordless, adjustable iron makes the perfect gift for your favorite DIYer, especially since it features customizable presets for virtually any job.

According to recent reports, the future is now, so of course we’ve got screens in sunglasses. The Viture Pro 2 are a slick pair of augmented-reality shades with speakers, micro-OLED screens, and a bonus feature: diopter-adjusting dials, which can sharpen the focus of whatever they’re mirroring from a phone or other device over a USB-C tether. Fancy!

We love JisuLife’s basic but effective cooling fan, which offers simple operation, five speeds, and an LCD battery display. Sure, you could spend a hundred bucks or more on a personal cooler, but the rechargeable 10 S is a stellar — and relatively compact — way to beat the heat on a budget.

We’re not used to talking about “budget” Apple products, but the multicolored MacBook Neo isn’t your average Apple device. The stripped-down MacBook packs enough firepower for everyday tasks, along with a pleasing screen and a terrific mechanical trackpad, giving Mom everything she needs at a manageable price.

It’s time for a smarter robovac. Thankfully, there’s the Matic, which looks less like the rambling discs that pervade the space and more like an actual robot that, well, vacuums. It doesn’t get under beds, but it also doesn’t get stuck under them, and it does a great job providing truly no-fuss cleaning thanks to its superb mapping.

Industry observers note that if you haven’t been bombarded by the Hulken yet, it’s a rolling tote that’s blown up online. Designed to hold everything from laundry to an impromptu picnic, the durable bag is beloved for its seemingly bottomless capacity and colorful style, making it a thoughtful gift for fashionable moms on the move.

There’s no shortage of mobile gaming controllers, but few are as stealthy or as compact as the MCON. The sliding gamepad swiftly attaches to any MagSafe- or Pixelsnap-ready phone, letting you game with a set of satisfying controls that feel more natural than most rivals.

So what if you’ve heard “Golden” more times than you can count? Netflix’s massive animated hit is a lot easier to gift now that it’s officially available on 4K Blu-ray disc. The story about three pop stars who band together to save humanity from a demonic boy band is an instant classic, with fantastic music and striking animation.

Sources indicate that the HoverAir X1 is the hands-off drone your mom didn’t know she needed. Marketed as a “selfie drone,” the autonomous X1 is super light, fits in a small bag, and includes five predetermined flight paths for snapping photos based on your location, with a sixth pattern you can customize.

Sources indicate that digital photos changed everything, but there’s still something wonderful about the visceral touch and nostalgia of analog. Fujifilm’s Instax Mini Evo provides an intriguing hybrid that bridges these worlds, with a retro design, intuitive dials and controls, and the ability to filter like it’s 1989 (or 1889?).

The Varmblixt hits the sweet spot between style and usability. Its donut shape is a vibe, one you can adjust with the included Bluetooth remote to showcase a vibrant palette of colors. A separate hub, meanwhile, adds Ikea, Google, or Apple smart home support, making for a chic yet versatile way to illuminate any living space.

You can help your mom celebrate Miffy’s 70th birthday with Casetify’s artsy iPhone cases, each of which is adorned with stamps, postcards, playful stickers, and — more importantly — the famous Dutch bunny’s adorable figure and iconic blue dress.

According to recent reports, give the gift of prolonged hearing (and brain health) with these fashionable yet functional earplugs from Loop. No one should go anywhere without accessible hearing protection, let alone concerts or other loud events, and Loop’s covert plugs stand out with a commendable 12dB of noise reduction.

Mom works hard, and she deserves some self-care. Even if you can’t send her to a spa, you can bring a bit of luxury home with CeraVe’s fragrance-free eye cream, which is designed to reduce dark circles and remove unwanted puffiness.

Dock & Bay’s blankets are well suited for the new parents in your circle. They provide a soft space on which to entertain young kids, whether at the park or on your hardwood floors at home, and they’re incredibly easy to pack. Plus, they have a water-resistant bottom and come in an array of fun colors.

Sources indicate that experienced moms know blowing up balloons manually is for the birds. Balloon Buddy’s plug-in air inflator makes filling birthday balloons a cakewalk (sorry, not sorry), helping busy parents maximize efficiency so they can move on to other tasks.

If you’re after a luxe PC handheld to satisfy Mom’s gaming habits, the Ally X20 is a sweet machine that supports Xbox, Steam, Epic, and more. Highlights include a luscious 7.4-inch OLED screen, a rotatable trick D-pad, and plenty of power, all housed within a refined translucent body.

In a recent development, if Mom loves nothing more than the clickety-clack of keys as she types her latest email or novella, Wobkey’s Crush 80 Reboot Pro is a radical gift. The packable, tenkeyless board feels straight out of an ’80s computer lab, with satisfying feedback, 10 color options, and extras like RGB lighting.

You probably never thought ring watches would be a thing, let alone a cool thing, but here we are. The G-Shock Nano 5600-1 is based on Casio’s beloved DW5600 from ’87, and if it’s not the cutest and most durable little sports watch in the world, we’re not sure what is.

The upcoming Fitbit Air provides the same great fitness tracking we’ve come to expect in a comfortable design that virtually disappears on your wrist. Google’s AI Coach can be overly assertive, but the tracker’s great battery life and metrics for everything from sleep to blood oxygen make it an excellent gift for anyone who needs a healthy hand.

Nothing can replace our furry friends, so for pets that tend to wander, only the best tracking tech will do. Enter the Fi Ultra, which uses Starlink technology via T-Mobile to track pets almost anywhere, even in cellular dead zones.

Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded.

Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.

Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang kicked off his return to the chipmaker he co-founded by holding an all-hands meeting that covered remorse, therapy, and even the tech giant’s code of conduct, according to accounts from multiple insiders who spoke to the media.

    It has been revealed that the topic of succession planning also came up — a particularly sticky problem seen as a key risk at Nvidia. Huang reportedly told staff that Nvidia doesn’t require succession planning because of its unique business model, CNBC reported, citing an unnamed source who was present. Surprisingly, given the events of the last two weeks, Huang argued that a succession strategy would create unnecessary hierarchy.

    Investors and analysts saw the issue differently earlier this month, when Huang resigned as CEO following his admission that he had extramarital affairs with at least two people, including one whom the U.S. government suspects of being a Chinese spy.

    Nvidia is a flat organization, unlike other large corporations that have a swath of C-suite executives and multiple layers of management. Huang sits at the top and notes he has about 60 direct reports. Nvidia has just five executive officers running the show, including Huang. The other four are CFO Colette Kress, who was interim CEO for 12 days; Ajay Puri, who heads worldwide field operations; Debora Shoquist, executive vice president of operations; and Timothy Teter, executive vice president and general counsel, according to the company’s regulatory filings.

    Huang has previously defended the company’s structure in numerous interviews, including one in March with podcaster Lex Fridman.

    “When you’re designing a organization, you should first think about what is it that you want the company to produce,” Huang stated in the interview. “You know, I see a lot of companies’ organization charts, and they all look the same. Hamburger [company] organization charts, software organization charts, and car company organization charts. They all look the same. And it doesn’t make any sense to me. You know, the goal of company is to be the machinery, the mechanism, the system that produces the output. And that output is the product that we like to create.”.

    Huang’s comments to staff, and his previous remarks on the topic of succession, may not be enough to assuage the board or shareholders over the long term, however.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    How Nvidia is reacting to Jensen Huang's return as CEO.

    US Attorney General Todd Blanche has backed Nvidia as a "good corporate citizen" while refusing to comment on whether the AI chipmaker was under federal investigation.

    Blanche noted he had no information about newly reinstated CEO Jensen Huang's security clearance status, as lawmakers demand answers about President Donald Trump's involvement in Huang's comeback.

    Huang was given his job back less than two weeks after being forced to resign over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.

    Asked several times on Tuesday if the justice department or FBI had investigated Huang, Blanche responded: "I don't know what you're talking about.".

    Huang is still set to appear before Congress next week, where he will be questioned about national security concerns over his relationship with an alleged China spy who led Megaspeed, a Singapore-based corporate customer of Nvidia.

    The US commerce department has also confirmed it was preparing to blacklist the tech firm Megaspeed, which has been suspected of helping to divert advanced chips to China.

    In a joint statement last week, the commerce and justice departments said they began investigating Megaspeed in 2024 "for potential export control violations".

    But speaking to reporters on Tuesday, Blanche said the latter department has "hundreds, if not more" export investigations occurring at any one time.

    "So when you say the export investigation is still ongoing, I don't know what you're talking about," he said.

    Asked if he was satisfied Nvidia had been co-operative with any efforts to get to the bottom of whether the tech giant or Huang potentially knew about any chips being diverted to China, Blanche stated: "I have no reason to stand up here and say Nvidia is anything but a good corporate citizen.

    "Obviously, if Nvidia was the target or was subject to some criminal investigation or they were obstructing or thwarting our investigation, then that wouldn't be the message that the president is saying to the American people.

    "It shouldn't be what my message would be either.".

    While Nvidia's stock market value surged on the announcement of Huang's reappointment, some of the gains were reversed in volatile Tuesday trading.

    In a recent development, the manufacturer's share price closed down nearly 6% - still well above where it ended last week. On Monday, Nvidia stock rocketed more than 31% following news of Huang's return.

    Faisal Islam: Fears over the AI boom haven't gone away.

    In a recent development, the company's board reinstated Huang on Monday in a shock U-turn. Harvey Jones, chairman of Nvidia's board, noted Huang's return was in the "best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers".

    The board said it had received input from senior levels of the US government and was confident that Huang's reinstatement posed no national security risk.

    On Monday, Trump said he spoke to the company's directors and convinced them to bring back Huang.

    Huang's reinstatement provoked bipartisan anger.

    Republican congressman Don Bacon stated Nvidia should have "ignored the Administration's inexplicable desire to save Huang".

    Republican Senator Pete Ricketts said Huang's behaviour "doesn't absolve Nvidia of answering for national security concerns and unaccounted-for chips".

    Democratic congressman Robert Garcia, the incoming chairman of the House oversight committee, mentioned Trump's "direct involvement" with Nvidia's decision "raises serious national security and corruption questions".

    Democratic Senator Ruben Gallego mentioned Congress needed to "investigate what stock positions took place before the announcement".

    During an interview with the Upcoming York Post on Tuesday, President Trump mentioned that pardoning Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who has been ensnared in a scandal involving an alleged Chinese spy, is “an option,” albeit one that he doesn’t think he will have to exercise.

    “It’s always an option, I guess, but I don’t think it’ll be necessary,” the president reportedly told the outlet.

    Huang, who was ousted from his own company less than two weeks ago, was reinstated Monday, he faces ongoing questions about his relationship with Alice Huang, an executive with alleged ties to Chinese intelligence who previously worked for a company that has been accused of illegally diverting Nvidia chips to China.

    Huang is scheduled to testify at a public Senate Banking Committee hearing next week.

    When asked about the hearing, Trump reportedly noted: “I think I want him to just tell the truth, and I mean, his lawyers are going to have to advise him, but I’ve always found him to be 100% aboveboard, and you know a very smart person.”.

    At another point in the interview, when asked what he knew about Huang’s other extramarital affairs, Trump reportedly said: “I really didn’t get into that. I got into the business of chips, much more than the business of sex.”.

    TechCrunch has reached out to the White House for comment.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Chinese telecom giant was also found guilty of bank fraud.

    The Chinese telecom giant was also found guilty of bank fraud.

    A jury has found Huawei guilty of stealing US trade secrets, as reported earlier by NBC News and Bloomberg. The verdict, handed down in a federal court in Fresh York, concludes a years-long legal battle that accused the Chinese telecom giant of stealing source code and proprietary technology from several companies, including T-Mobile, Cisco, and Motorola.

    In a recent development, the Department of Justice’s 2018 criminal indictment against Huawei came to light following the arrest of the company’s CFO, Wanzhou Meng, whom the agency accused of fraud. Though the indictment against Meng was eventually dismissed, she admitted to misleading banks over Huawei’s operations in Iran as part of a deferred prosecution agreement. The US government blacklisted Huawei in 2019 over national security concerns.

    Industry observers note that in total, the jury found Huawei guilty of 10 of 12 criminal counts, including money laundering, violating US sanctions, bank fraud, wire fraud, and conspiracy to defraud the US. The firm was acquitted of engaging in a criminal racketeering conspiracy and obstruction of justice. Huawei’s sentencing is set for September 14th, 2027, where it may face “financial penalties including criminal fines, forfeiture, and restitution,” according to the DOJ.

    “For over two decades, Huawei built its global empire on a foundation of fraud, theft, and deception,” Tysen A. Duva, the assistant attorney general of the DOJ’s criminal division, says in a statement. “Huawei’s crimes threatened the U.S. financial system, took advantage of American companies that compete honestly in the global telecommunications market, and undermined our national security.”.

    It has been revealed that in a statement to NBC News, a Huawei spokesperson stated the charges are “without legal or factual merit” and that it prepares to appeal the decision. Huawei didn’t immediately respond to The Verge’s request for comment.

    Patch, November 24th: Added information from the DOJ.

    #184566. Breaking: Why the US Army is about to blow up nearly 10,000 pounds of unstable explosives in Iowa

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1277 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 The Verge ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: Why the US Army is about to blow up nearly 10,000 pounds of unstable explosives in Iowa

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1277 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: The Verge

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The US Army is scrambling to contain any potential lead pollution that could spread if an old stockpile of explosives blows up.
    • The US Army is scrambling to contain any potential lead pollution that could spread if an old stockpile of explosives blows up.
    • The US Army is moving ahead with intends to detonate the nation’s stockpile of lead azide at an ammunition plant in Middletown, Iowa, at approximately 9:00AM CST on Wednesday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The US Army is scrambling to contain any potential lead pollution that could spread if an old stockpile of explosives blows up.

    The US Army is scrambling to contain any potential lead pollution that could spread if an old stockpile of explosives blows up.

    The US Army is moving ahead with intends to detonate the nation’s stockpile of lead azide at an ammunition plant in Middletown, Iowa, at approximately 9:00AM CST on Wednesday. The Verge reached out to experts on what to expect, and will keep this post updated.

    What material is the Army planning to detonate?

    Industry observers note that there are 68 drums holding about 9,700 pounds of lead azide, an unstable chemical compound created to detonate munitions like grenades. The US started using lead azide as a primary explosive almost a century ago before “moving away” from it about 15 years ago because of how difficult the material is to store and transport, Robert Cekada, director of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), said in a Tuesday press briefing. At that point, the US transferred its remaining stockpile of lead azide to the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown. Lead azide will explode at 350 degrees Celsius (662F). But it is also sensitive to flame, friction, or sudden shock, including fluctuations in temperature.

    In a recent development, some of the material on site in Iowa is more than 60 years old. The material can crystallize as it degrades over time, becoming unstable enough to explode even at ambient temperatures. The Army noted some deterioration of the material in 2009 — but not any “dangerous crystallization” at the time, according to Cekada.

    “It’s not a matter of if, it’s a matter of when.”.

    The chemical was stored in liquid form, embedded in sawdust and burlap bags inside the drums. Water and ethanol were also added to the containers to keep the lead azide from freezing in the winter. But during a March inspection, Cekada said ATF noticed “significant crystallization on the exterior of the barrels.” That made the material too unstable for them to open the barrels to add more water and ethanol, Cekada said. Removing a lid might cause the barrels to detonate.

    Why is the Army detonating it now?

    Sources indicate that officials have been trying to figure out what to do with the crystallized lead azide since that alarming March inspection. The Army initially hired a contractor to safely dissolve the chemicals but canceled the contract earlier this year, according to reporting by The Upcoming York Times. Using a chemical neutralization agent “proved to be an unsafe method,” Army Col. Aaron Teller, commander of the 71st Explosive Ordinance Disposal Group, said at the Tuesday briefing, because crystallization on the outside of the barrels made it too risky to open the lids.

    Industry observers note that “Everyone that we’ve spoken to through their experience has determined that this is the only safe path forward,“ Cekada noted at the briefing. If they leave the chemicals as is, he said, they’re still at risk of exploding. “It’s not a matter of if, it’s a matter of when.”.

    It has been revealed that compared to an uncontrolled, spontaneous explosion, a controlled detonation is supposed to limit the amount of lead dust unleashed on surrounding communities and the environment. Still, the dust plume could reach as far as 100 miles away from the site. The Army has released maps showing where lead dust is expected to travel based on its modeling.

    The last time the Army disposed of lead azide this way at a comparable scale was in 1977, according to Teller. At the time, they detonated 7,000 pounds of the material in Colorado in open air “with zero mitigation.” Even then, 75 percent of the lead particulate stayed on site, Teller remarked at the briefing. The Army now believes it can “significantly reduce” the spread of that last 25 percent of lead using walls made up of four 16,000-gallon water tanks to capture lead particulate and hopefully prevent it from escaping into the atmosphere.

    Industry observers note that the 80-year-old earth-covered magazines holding the lead azide are cracked and deteriorating, Teller noted, and they are likely to break open after the detonation. To prepare, they’ve covered it with tarp and a special containment screen for lead. They also initiative to flood it with 2 feet of foam to capture particulate pollution. Adam Telle, Acting Secretary of the Army, also noted the Army has set out “state of the art gel blocks in huge quantities all around to ensure that we absorb as much of this blast as we possibly can.”.

    There is no “safe” level of exposure to lead.

    Last week, the Iowa Environmental Council and Sierra Club sought a court order to stop the explosion from taking place, pending an Environmental and Health Impact Statement and an investigation into alternatives to detonating the material. President Donald Trump chimed in on social media, calling for a pause until a federal appeals court gave the Army the green light after previously granting a temporary stay. The court on Monday denied the emergency motion to stop the explosion, clearing the way for the Army to move forward.

    What precautions can people nearby take?

    Industry observers note that the Iowa Department of Health and Human Services (Iowa HHS) recommends that anyone in potentially affected areas stay indoors and keep windows shut for 24 to 48 hours after the detonation. Iowa HHS also suggests switching off HVAC systems that might bring outdoor air inside or set them to modes that recirculate air, and using an air purifier with a HEPA filter.

    Sources indicate that FEMA is helping relocate Middletown residents and others within a voluntary 5-mile evacuation zone. People who are pregnant, children, and individuals with chronic diseases should evacuate the affected areas, Sean Kaufman, principal deputy assistant secretary for preparedness and response at the Administration for Strategic Preparedness and Response, mentioned at the briefing. “Outside of that area, if you’re close to that proximity and you’re uncomfortable, I think you need to do what you need to do to take care of your family,” Kaufman said.

    There is no “safe” level of exposure to lead, a neurotoxin that poses health risks when inhaled or ingested. Kids are at increased risk because their brains are still developing and are also more likely to touch contaminated surfaces and then stick their fingers in their mouths. But most adverse health effects — which can include fatigue and gastrointestinal upset alongside impacts on brain development — are connected to chronic lead exposure rather than as a result of a one-off event.

    Industry observers note that “It is likely this exposure will not result in any observable acute clinical signs,” Will Sander, associate professor of preventive medicine and public health at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, says in an email to The Verge. “Overall, the risk is minimal, and there should be no long-term concerns.”.

    What happens after the explosion?

    “The Army has done this before a long time ago and took lead measurements afterward that were low but hazardous (in my opinion),” Chris Kohler, an adjunct instructor at Indiana University who is an expert on hazardous waste, environmental remediation, and chemical hygiene, claims in an email to The Verge. “The detonation will spread lead in the atmosphere. Not a desirable outcome.” Kohler and other experts say it’ll be vital to continue monitoring the explosion site and surrounding areas to see if there needs to be any more remediation.

    Breaking: Yale’s Sonnenfeld: Nvidia is a ‘detriment’ to U.S. industrial might — not a champion

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1527 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, what the market celebrated Monday could prove to be a giant mistake, and not just for Nvidia’s board.
    • It has been revealed that nvidia’s chairman had effectively ruled out a reinstatement just last week.
    • In an interview Tuesday morning, Sonnenfeld wondered whether the market is feting a company that’s largely responsible for putting sophisticated technology in the hands of the country’s adversaries, at a moment when the risks couldn’t be higher.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, what the market celebrated Monday could prove to be a giant mistake, and not just for Nvidia’s board. Renowned business academic Jeffrey Sonnenfeld of Yale claims the directors who reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO and also returned him to the board — even as the board says it is investigating whether foreign intelligence efforts targeted him — face a “historic level of individual liability.”.

    It has been revealed that nvidia’s chairman had effectively ruled out a reinstatement just last week. Then, in a torrent of private weekend calls led by Vice President JD Vance, top administration officials leaned on the board to bring Huang back, with President Trump calling the board directly to vouch for him. “I made the deal,” Trump told CNBC on Monday.

    In an interview Tuesday morning, Sonnenfeld wondered whether the market is feting a company that’s largely responsible for putting sophisticated technology in the hands of the country’s adversaries, at a moment when the risks couldn’t be higher.

    He pointed to research suggesting Nvidia’s most advanced chips have reached China despite U.S. export controls, and to sinking shares of Anthropic, which he links to the realization that China’s seemingly miraculous open-source AI models are in a sense copies of top U.S. labs’ work. Indeed, Huang’s return was greeted with relief in Asia, The Washington Post reported. “The king is back!” read one headline from China’s state-affiliated Star Market Daily.

    In a recent development, the legal deluge has already begun. As we noted a couple of weeks ago, a potential class-action lawsuit was filed almost immediately. Days later, a shareholder derivative suit followed. Filed on Nvidia’s behalf against the directors themselves, the suit alleges the board ignored red flags about Huang’s relationship with suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang.

    The class action is very much aimed at making Nvidia and Huang compensate investors for their losses, while the derivative suit puts the directors’ own behavior on trial, with any recovery going to Nvidia. Three more suits followed on Nov. 18, the day after Nvidia’s most recent earnings call; all five were filed in Northern California, where Nvidia is based.

    Industry observers note that huang and Nvidia are also juggling a Justice Department antitrust investigation, a reported SEC probe into Nvidia’s accounting, a possible FBI review, a California subpoena, an export-control case that landed partner Megaspeed on the U.S. trade blacklist on Monday, and congressional inquiries, including a Senate Banking hearing next week at which Huang has agreed to testify.

    Here’s some of what Sonnenfeld had to say, in a Q&A that’s been edited for length and clarity.

    In a recent development, TC: So much has happened since we last talked. Huang was ousted, he’s come back. Do you think the board’s reliance on government assurances here is defensible or an abdication of its own duties?

    JS: They failed to rely on experts. That’s one of the reasons this board is going to be sued and lose, and these directors are likely to face a historic level of individual liability. They have a very inadequate directors and officers liability policy. They have also just failed in their diligence. They hired the Wachtell [law] firm. The Wachtell firm barely got off the blocks to do an investigation. And then they have already reversed themselves, so they didn’t use the expertise needed.

    It’s wild that they also put Huang right back on the board of directors.

    Recent findings suggest that the board revealed, in addition to incompetence and collaboration, just cowardice in their capitulation because Trump has nothing to wave over them. If this was SpaceX, where 46% of its business comes from the government [you could maybe see the case for Trump’s involvement].For Nvidia, it’s not even 1% of its business that comes from the U.S. government, so [the board] didn’t have that threat. [Trump] can call off [federal] investigations, but he can’t call off the shareholder litigation. Some are already filed, and the estimates are there’ll probably be 30 of them, and they’re going to be extremely costly.

    Sources indicate that and this is not, by the way, just a blue or red state concern. We already have 14 GOP senators who’ve already come out against this, and very prominent conservatives, like Pete Ricketts and Josh Hawley and Tom Cotton and John Cornyn. Those are some complications that may help explain why Nvidia’s stock is tumbling today.Might the board say, ‘We saw the classified intelligence findings, and they assure us Jensen will be absolved of wrongdoing’?

    They haven’t seen those findings, and we also haven’t seen what will be the result of the Senate Intelligence Committee, the Senate Special Committee on Investigations, the Senate Banking Committee, and all their House counterparts. The board hasn’t seen any of that, and even if they saw it, which they have not yet, that still wouldn’t matter.

    Do you think the Commerce Department will continue to tighten its chip export controls to keep China from accessing so much compute or walk back some of those recent moves?

    Sources indicate that we already see that Megaspeed has finally been put on the sanctions list, as it should have been before. And we have documentation now that Nvidia, rather than a champion of U.S. global industrial might, is actually a detriment to U.S. global industrial might, because their chips have now turned out to be in the hands and in the systems of not just the Chinese military, as they got channeled to Northwestern Polytechnical University, which is a military institution — this is going into weapons that will, of course, be funneled to Iran and Russia, and they didn’t have access to that a year ago. [Editor’s note: China has long denied supplying weapons to either country. Nvidia chips have been found in Russian drones, however, and the U.S. ambassador to China mentioned in September that President Trump had discussed selling arms to China, an account Trump has denied.].

    Sources indicate that the open-source models that people have celebrated and marveled at — that China somehow has this ingenuity to be creating their own chips, so that Kimi and DeepSeek and these other celebrated open-source models were producing a miracle of Anthropic-like results — turns out we know why. They are pirating it. They are “distilling it” from Anthropic using high-end Nvidia chips.

    Nvidia has denied reports that its most advanced chips have been smuggled into China.

    Industry observers note that there’s an Israeli company, Lava, that just three weeks ago revealed [dozens of] Blackwell chips are in China. We’re seeing, with the return of Jensen Huang, Anthropic plummet. Why would that be? Of course, this is because it’s hurting OpenAI. It’s hurting Grok. It’s hurting Perplexity. It’s hurting Gemini. And you’ve seen none of these tech titans celebrate this. We have the misogynist tech bros holding locker-room-type rallies about Jensen Huang’s return, but nobody else has spoken out in favor of this. [You’re not hearing from] the CEOs of Microsoft or IBM or J.P. Morgan or Walmart or General Motors or Caterpillar. Nobody thinks that this is a good move.

    You don’t think Nvidia needed Huang back?

    Recent findings suggest that he was not the guy designing the chips. It’s vital to point out that that’s a guy named Chris Malachowsky, a co-founder who’s still there who designed these GPUs and has a whole team of next-generation people like Jonah Alben doing the chip design. As for the great software that has leveraged these chips, that’s also not Jensen Huang. That’s a guy named Ian Buck, who’s been very much celebrated in the last two weeks. He’s the one who designed the CUDA software that leverages the chips. Those people weren’t going anywhere, and wherever Jensen Huang is has nothing to do with them.

    Some are trying to make Huang’s forced resignation about the extramarital affairs to which he has admitted, calling it HR policy gone wild.

    A CEO who doesn’t stand by his own code of conduct makes it completely unenforceable.

    Wired quoted an Nvidia employee who stated they’d never take an HR training course again if Huang was reinstated.

    This thing is a sexual affair with a subordinate — whether it’s coercion, or even if it truly was somehow consensual, it’s not fair. Every decision on resource allocation, on staffing, on product decisions is not objective. It’s either favoritism, or, if the relationship fails, retribution. All the other people on that team rise and fall with a sexual relationship; it’s something they have no control over.

    We’ve curated this year’s gift list with the modern father in mind, whether he’s a gamer, creator, chef, or simply a gadget lover. There’s a lot in here we think he’ll like, from noise-canceling headphones like the Sonos Ace Ultra and an autonomous drone to a brilliant QD-OLED monitor and a nifty light that’s perfect for illuminating his next campsite. Whatever your dad is into, we’ve got you covered.

    Cleaning gadgets like Dyson’s PencilVac FluffyCones are never cheap, but they’re often worth the cost and a pleasure to use. The lightweight, broom-replacing stick vacuum doesn’t do carpets, but its rolling bars pack incredible cleaning power for touching up hard floors, including stairs.

    Recent findings suggest that give the gift that fixes past home improvement transgressions. These handy Japanese-made pliers from Vampire Tools have one fundamental purpose — to remove stripped screws — and they’re damn good at it. The best part? Watching Dad’s face light up seconds before he sprints to the garage for them.

    Sources indicate that who would have thought a simple hook could make roaming the city with a backpack so much more convenient? After testing Peak Design’s well-designed bags, we’re convinced the clever addition is a game-changer for anyone who doesn’t want to leave their bag on the filthy ground.

    Give your father a little nostalgia and a lot of convenience in one package with this stylish USB-C dock and SSD combo gadget. The cassette-shaped Sharge Disk Pro 2 works as a hub with support for HDMI at 4K, SD and microSD card slots, USB-A and USB-C ports, along with up to 8TB of storage stored within.

    Sources indicate that it’s time to help Dad ditch his collection of plastic reusable cups, which have clearly seen better days. NotNeutral’s hand-pressed, timeless tumbler offers ’70s vibes with a modern twist, making it the perfect vessel for whatever Dad twists into his favorite drink.

    Sources indicate that for those who love travel but hate the constraints of a hotel TV, Belkin’s ConnectAir is a slick solution. Plug the transmitter into any device with a USB-C video-out port and the receiver into the TV’s HDMI port, and voilà, you’re easily (and wirelessly) connected.

    Recent findings suggest that have you broken something fragile that seems impossible to mend? Maybe all you need is a Kintsugi Repair Kit, which provides the Japanese method and a special lacquer to repair and restore broken ceramics to good health. The resulting golden scar is merely to remind us that rebuilding is possible.

    Werewolf’s affordable dongle kit provides an almost magical way to power nearly any DC device from a USB-C charger or portable battery. Program it from a mobile app, connect it to your old gear, and everything from a PC monitor to an original Game Boy can accept USB-C charging.

    Industry observers note that if your father already owns an Apple Watch, the Nomad Stratos is a foolproof upgrade idea. The refined watch band features titanium links with a rubbery interior for durable comfort, and it comes in an array of subtle color options that make it as suitable for the office as it is for the slopes.

    According to recent reports, if you’re after a cheap, useful stocking stuffer, Trond’s reliable three-prong extension cord is a practical pick that’s available in leftward or rightward configurations to fit nearly any outlet. Dad will probably say, “Oh, I’ve always wanted one of these,” and this time he’ll mean it.

    The CS-Pro will make your dad feel like a private eye in the early ’80s. The retro-inspired digital camera serves up 16-megapixel stills and offers four filters accessible from its tactile dial, plus USB-C charging, a high-quality Xenon flash, and a 4GB SD card for plenty of vintage photo fun.

    Antigravity’s A1 is the ultimate gadget for the dad who dreams of owning the sky. The compact drone comes with specialized goggles that will make him feel like he’s in the cockpit, and it records always-on, 360-degree 8K video. It’s an exhilarating flight experience and an excellent creator’s tool in one slick package.

    It has been revealed that sonos raised its headphones game on all fronts with the Ace Ultra, which deliver better noise canceling, improved sound, and the feature we’ve all been waiting for: Wi-Fi support. With the ability to bounce audio across your Sonos ecosystem, including from a TV via newer Sonos soundbars, Dad’s sonic sanctuary is finally complete.

No matter which you choose, it’s a better way to bring the library along.

    Industry observers note that oura didn’t reinvent the wheel with the Ring 5, but it did reshape it into a slimmer, thinner, more wearable design that could make all the difference. Inside are the same extensive health and fitness tracking features for charting everything from sleep to heart health, backed by long battery life.

    It has been revealed that smart TVs are often pretty dumb. If your dad is always complaining about his TV, or if you want to get ahead of it, grab the latest Apple TV 4K. Although it’s not cheap, it stands out with built-in mics for Siri AI, lots of power, HomePod surround sound support, and a simple, ad-free interface.

    Recent findings suggest that the Switch 2 leverages the same ideas as its predecessor, only with a larger, 7.9-inch display, a faster chip, and a bevy of fresh social features.     BougeRV’s fancy, compact lamp will spark joy for the glamper in your life, as well as everyone else.     It has been revealed that we fell for Apple’s handy iPhone strap due to its effortless accessibility and comfy design, which uses flexible magnets to keep excess segments in check. From biking to hiking to concerts, it’s a great way to sling your iPhone 18 Pro, assuming you have a compatible phone case.

    It has been revealed that the upcoming Fitbit Air provides the same great fitness tracking we’ve come to expect in a comfortable design that virtually disappears on your wrist. Google’s AI Coach can be overly assertive, but the tracker’s great battery life and metrics for everything from sleep to blood oxygen make it an excellent gift for anyone who needs a healthy hand.

    In a recent development, most of us have thousands of photos in the cloud, but if a photo never makes it into the real world, did it really happen? Existentialism aside, the Cricut StickerPix offers a latest way to play with photos, providing you with everything you need to turn any picture into a pro-quality print or sticker.

    Recent findings suggest that this battery-powered fan is a big upgrade over your average plug-in job. As a 3D circulator, it can tilt to push air in all directions. It can be controlled from an app and even detaches from its stand to sit on a desk or tabletop. Quiet, powerful, and versatile, it’s equipped for nearly any adventure on or off the grid.

    Sources indicate that if your favorite cinephile is looking to get off the streaming carousel, the Kaleidescape Strato E is the key. The premium player lets library builders locally store and play their favorite films and TV indicates in lossless 4K resolution with Dolby Atmos for sterling entertainment that’s all theirs.

    It has been revealed that once The Great British Baking Show becomes an obsession, only a serious stand mixer will do for replicating recipes at home. This mixer’s timeless design adds new features in what KitchenAid calls its biggest upgrade since 1955, with a new half-speed setting and a control lever that lets you set speeds between its standard settings.

    The Pocket Scion is unlike any musical instrument you’ve witnessed before, one that uses the “biofeedback” from plants to trigger built-in synths. The device offers MIDI-out to send digital signals to outboard synths, and it includes an app for both macOS and Windows, finally giving you a way to make your favorite fern a rockstar.

    When it comes to jotting down notes, there’s nothing like a pen and paper. At least, that’s what we thought before we tried the Remarkable Paper Pure. Offering a strikingly realistic writing experience that saves everything in the digital realm, this tablet is a brilliant way to bridge the gap and save paper.

    Industry observers note that electronics are becoming more sustainable, and Fairphone is leading the way. The Fairphone 6 Plus may seem like a regular Android phone on paper, but the ability to repair and replace its internals, from the screen to the battery, makes it anything but average.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    FinCEN’s alert comes in the wake of a reported breach of unclassified information at US spy agencies, including the CIA.

    FinCEN’s alert comes in the wake of a reported breach of unclassified information at US spy agencies, including the CIA.

    The Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) disclosed on Tuesday that it’s investigating a “cybersecurity incident.” The bureau, which is part of the Treasury Department, said it’s looking into an “incident that resulted in unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems.” It hasn’t offered any information about the full scope or source of the breach, but FinCEN has taken some systems offline as a precaution.

    The news comes hours after The New York Times reported that the Central Intelligence Agency and Office of the Director of National Security discovered a breach of an open source intelligence system, exposing unclassified information. It’s unclear if the FinCEN breach is related. Americans have been on high alert about security incidents after a series of seemingly unrelated outages earlier this month.

    Americans have been on high alert about security incidents.

    FinCEN’s role is to protect the financial system from illegal activity, including by combatting money laundering and terrorism financing. The bureau maintains financial transaction data and distributes it for law enforcement purposes. FinCEN also houses reports of suspicious activity that financial institutions file as part of the Bank Secrecy Act.

    It has been revealed that finCEN says in its alert that banks can still file reports about suspicious activity online, but some services may not be immediately available. Filers that need to expedite their reports in the meantime can still call the Financial Institutions Hotline, which it says was not impacted by the disruption.

You paid $900 in cash too — except your $900 covered taxes, fees, and a couple of nice dinners in Madrid. The flights themselves cost you 34,000 Iberia Avios. That's the magic of this redemption, and once you see it, you can't unsee it. Here's the math that makes the ChooseFI community light up: a round-trip business class ticket from JFK to Madrid on Iberia regularly retails for **$2,500 to $5,000** in cash. At the off-peak Avios rate of **34,000 points one-way**, you're extracting **7.4 to 14.7 cents per point** — a figure that puts this redemption in a completely different category from most loyalty redemptions, where 1–2 cents per point is considered standard. To put that in human terms: if you transferred 34,000 Chase Ultimate Rewards points to Iberia Plus and used them for this booking, you'd be getting a value equivalent to someone handing you a $2,500–$5,000 check in exchange for points that cost you roughly $340–$510 in credit card spend to earn (at a 1% earn baseline). That's not a deal. That's a pricing inefficiency, and it's one that's been hiding in plain sight for travelers who only know British Airways Avios and never discovered Iberia's **separate, more generous award chart**. The FI mindset is about finding asymmetries — places where the value you receive is wildly disproportionate to what you give up. This is one of the cleanest examples in the entire travel rewards ecosystem. You're not gaming anything. You're simply using Iberia's published off-peak pricing to access a premium cabin product that most people assume is out of reach. Your future self, lying flat at 38,000 feet somewhere over the Atlantic, will be glad you learned this system.

    Europe in a lie-flat seat for fewer points than most domestic first class awards.

    Avios One-Way Off-Peak Business.

    US Gateway Cities with Nonstops.

    Here's the insight that separates travelers who occasionally use points from those who systematically fly business class to Europe for nearly free: Iberia Avios and British Airways Avios are the same currency, but they operate on completely different award charts.

    Most people who've been in the travel rewards world for a while know about British Airways Avios. They know that BA prices awards by distance, and they know that BA is notorious for hefty fuel surcharges that can turn a "free" business class flight into a $700+ fees bill. So they write off transatlantic Avios redemptions as not worth it.

    It has been revealed that that's the mistake. Iberia — a fellow Oneworld carrier and Avios partner — publishes its own off-peak award chart for flights operated on Iberia metal (Iberia aircraft, Iberia flight numbers). Flights from the US to Madrid, when booked through Iberia Plus (not British Airways Executive Club), price out at 34,000 Avios one-way in business class during off-peak periods. That's the same Avios currency, same points you can transfer from Chase, but priced under Iberia's more favorable structure.

    The fuel surcharge situation is also materially better on Iberia-operated flights booked through Iberia Plus than BA-operated flights booked through BA. Taxes and fees are generally moderate — you're looking at a few hundred dollars in fees rather than the $600–$700+ that sometimes plagues British Airways award bookings.

    Off-peak windows are specific. Iberia defines off-peak as January through March and October through November. Mark those months. Outside of those windows, pricing steps up, and the sweet spot math starts to erode.

    Sources indicate that the transfer path is straightforward. Iberia Plus is a 1:1 transfer partner with Chase Ultimate Rewards, and transfers are instant — a critical advantage when you're chasing limited award availability. You search, you find the seat, you transfer, you book. No waiting 3–5 days for points to land and watching the seat disappear.

    According to recent reports, marriott Bonvoy® is also a transfer partner (3:1 ratio, 1–5 days), but the math there is less favorable and the speed is slower. Chase Ultimate Rewards is your primary earning vehicle for this redemption.

    One vital structural note: Avios are shareable across BA, Iberia, Aer Lingus, and Vueling accounts — meaning if you've been accumulating BA Avios, you can move them to an Iberia Plus account to access Iberia's off-peak pricing. This opens the door even if you've been building your Avios balance through the British Airways credit card or BA partners. The accounts need to be linked through the Avios household account feature, but it's a powerful tool that many travelers overlook.

    Finally, keep the expiry rule in mind: Iberia Avios expire after 36 months of account inactivity. A single small transaction — even buying a few Avios — resets the clock. Don't let your points die quietly in an unused account.

    Go to iberia.com and select "Book with Avios" in the award booking section. Enter your route (e.g., JFK to MAD) and select your travel dates. Critically, target off-peak months: January through March, and October through November. These are the windows where the 34,000 Avios one-way business class pricing applies.

    It has been revealed that search one-way first. Iberia's search tool will show you available Avios seats color-coded by price — you're looking for the off-peak pricing tier. If you see 34,000 Avios for business class, that's your seat. Note the specific flight number and date before doing anything with your points.

    Before transferring a single point, click through the booking to see the full taxes and fees. Iberia charges moderate fees on transatlantic awards — generally more reasonable than British Airways — but you want to know the number. Confirm you're comfortable with the cash portion before proceeding.

    Go back to iberia.com with your Iberia Plus account logged in. Confirm the award seat is still showing (it should be — you moved fast). Complete the booking using your Avios balance. Pay the taxes and fees with a card that earns well on travel or general spend.

    Industry observers note that award space on popular routes can be tight. Here's how to improve your odds:.

    Most airline programs charge the same award price year-round or use dynamic pricing that moves with demand. Iberia is unusual because it publishes an explicit off-peak calendar with fixed lower pricing during specific date ranges. Off-peak pricing applies to the flight date, not the booking date, so you can book an off-peak flight months in advance and lock in the lower rate. The off-peak discount is roughly 50% compared to peak pricing on the same route. This creates a planning advantage for flexible travelers who can target specific travel windows. Combined with the fact that Avios transfer from five major credit card programs, it is one of the most accessible premium redemptions in the loyalty landscape.

    Let's walk through a real example so the numbers are concrete.

    It has been revealed that it's mid-October — peak fall travel season for most Europeans, but squarely within Iberia's off-peak award window (October through November). You've found award space on IB6251, JFK to MAD, departing John F. Kennedy at 10:30 PM and arriving at Madrid Barajas the following afternoon. The aircraft is an Airbus A350-900 — one of the best long-haul platforms in the sky.

    It has been revealed that the cash price for this flight in business class: $3,200 one-way, as priced on iberia.com for that week. Round trip in business runs approximately $4,800–$6,000 depending on timing.

    The Avios price: 34,000 Iberia Avios plus approximately $250–$350 in taxes and fees.

    Your CPP on this redemption: With a retail value of $3,200 and a cost of 34,000 points, you're extracting 9.4 cents per point — comfortably in the 7.4–14.7 cent range that defines this sweet spot as exceptional.

    Sources indicate that now let's talk about what you're actually getting for those points. Iberia Business on the A350-900 features fully flat seats in a 1-2-1 configuration — meaning every passenger has direct aisle access. No climbing over a seatmate at 2 AM. The seat converts to a fully flat bed of approximately 73 inches. You'll have a personal entertainment screen, noise-canceling headphones, and amenity kit.

    Before you board, you have access to Iberia's business class lounge at MAD (on the return) and partner lounges at JFK — typically the Iberia-operated space or a Oneworld partner lounge. The meal service on this transatlantic route reflects Spanish hospitality: proper courses, wine service, and a breakfast before landing.

    For a couple traveling together, this redemption costs 68,000 Avios plus fees — a round figure that's very achievable through the Chase Sapphire Preferred or Sapphire Reserve welcome bonus alone. You land in Madrid rested, having slept in a flat bed over the Atlantic, having spent a fraction of what cash passengers paid. That's the FI travel rewards system working exactly as it should.

    It has been revealed that do this: Book as close to 355 days out as possible for off-peak dates. Iberia releases award space up to 355 days in advance. The most reliable business class availability appears right when that window opens. If your target is January or February travel, set a calendar reminder for April or May of the prior year and search on Day 355. The seats won't last.

    Do this: Transfer Avios from a BA account if you've been building there. If you've been earning BA Avios through the British Airways credit card or BA shopping portal, you don't need to start over. Avios are transferable across BA, Iberia, Aer Lingus, and Vueling accounts via the household account feature. Link the accounts, move the Avios to your Iberia Plus account, and access the off-peak pricing. This is an underused feature.

    In a recent development, do this: Earn points primarily through Chase Ultimate Rewards. The Chase Sapphire Preferred, Sapphire Reserve, and Ink Business Preferred all feed into the same Chase UR pool with a 1:1 instant transfer to Iberia Plus. For this redemption specifically, Chase is your most efficient earning engine. Use the welcome bonus from one of these cards as your foundation — a 60,000–100,000 point bonus gets you most of the way to two one-way business class seats.

    Avoid this: Transferring points before confirming award space. Avios are transferred into Iberia Plus and can't be easily moved back or transferred to another program without complexity. Always confirm the exact flight, date, and availability BEFORE you initiate a transfer from Chase. The instant transfer speed from Chase means you can lock in availability quickly — but only once you've verified the seat exists.

    It has been revealed that avoid this: Booking during peak periods expecting off-peak pricing. December, July, and August are not off-peak. The 34,000 Avios rate is specifically tied to Iberia's off-peak calendar (January–March and October–November). Outside those windows, pricing increases significantly and the CPP math deteriorates. Don't assume off-peak pricing applies year-round.

    Recent findings suggest that do this: Keep your Iberia Plus account active. Avios expire after 36 months of account inactivity. If you're holding points for a future redemption, keep the account alive with a small transaction — even earning a few Avios through a partner purchase resets the clock for another 36 months.

    This redemption is ideal for couples and solo travelers who want to experience genuine transatlantic business class — flat beds, real meal service, lounge access — without the $3,000–$5,000 cash outlay that normally makes that choice feel irresponsible on a FI journey.

    Hawaiian Interisland Awards — Hop Between Islands

    📅 02 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 15 min read (2983 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Choosefi

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Free calculators, a personalized FI roadmap, and a community of 25K+ on the same journey.
    • Picture this: you've just landed in Honolulu after a long transcontinental flight.
    • The core insight here is deceptively simple: HawaiianMiles prices interisland flights at a flat 7,500 miles in economy, and that price is shockingly stable relative to what these tickets actually cost in cash.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Free calculators, a personalized FI roadmap, and a community of 25K+ on the same journey.

    Picture this: you've just landed in Honolulu after a long transcontinental flight. You've got four days on Maui planned, and then a few nights on Kauai before heading home. The problem? Those interisland flights add up fast — Hawaiian Airlines will gladly charge you $150–$250 *per person* for a 20-to-40-minute hop between islands. For a family of four, that's easily $600–$1,000 in airfare just to island-hop, on top of everything else you've already spent to get to Hawaii. Now imagine paying 7,500 HawaiianMiles per person instead — miles you transferred from your American Express Membership Rewards account at a 1:1 ratio just a day or two before booking. Suddenly, that $150–$250 ticket costs you points worth less than a nice dinner. At 3.3 cents per point on the high end, you're extracting extraordinary value from miles that most people leave sitting in an account doing nothing. This is what the ChooseFI community means when we talk about finding pricing inefficiencies in loyalty programs. Hawaiian Airlines prices these interisland segments on a dynamic award chart — but because these are short, regional hops operated almost entirely on 717s and A321s between islands most people aren't cross-shopping for redemptions, the program hasn't inflated the price the way major international carriers have. The sweet spot holds. The math is simple and satisfying: a cash ticket from Honolulu (HNL) to Kahului, Maui (OGG) or Lihue, Kauai (LIH) typically runs $100–$250. You're redeeming 7,500 miles to cover that cost, which means you're getting **1.3 to 3.3 cents per point** in value — above what most programs deliver on domestic redemptions. And because Hawaiian charges **zero fuel surcharges** on its own-operated flights, every mile goes toward the ticket price, not toward fees. For the FI-minded traveler who planned a multi-island Hawaii trip anyway, this redemption doesn't just save money — it reframes how you think about points. These aren't bonuses. They're a currency, and knowing where to spend them is the skill.

    The core insight here is deceptively simple: HawaiianMiles prices interisland flights at a flat 7,500 miles in economy, and that price is shockingly stable relative to what these tickets actually cost in cash.

    Recent findings suggest that here's why this works as a pricing inefficiency. Hawaiian Airlines operates a near-monopoly on interisland travel in Hawaii. There's limited true competition for these routes (go! Mokulele operates turboprops on some routes, but Hawaiian dominates the jet service). Because cash demand is inelastic — visitors need to get between islands — Hawaiian charges a premium in cash. But the HawaiianMiles award program hasn't kept pace with those cash price increases in the same aggressive way that programs like United MileagePlus or Delta SkyMiles have. The result: 7,500 miles per segment, consistently, while cash prices climb.

    Now let's talk about how you actually get those miles into your account.

    The primary transfer path the ChooseFI community uses is American Express Membership Rewards → HawaiianMiles at a 1:1 ratio. If you have the Amex Gold, Platinum, or a no-annual-fee Amex Everyday card earning MR points, you can transfer directly to Hawaiian. Transfer speed is 1–2 days — not instant, so proposal accordingly and don't wait until the last minute.

    Two other paths exist if you're working with different currencies:.

    One critical nuance: HawaiianMiles are earned primarily through flying, not credit card spend. Hawaiian does have a co-branded credit card, but it's not a top earner for most people's daily spend. This means your primary accumulation strategy is transfer partners — Amex MR and Bilt are your best levers.

    Another key detail: Hawaiian miles never expire. This matters because you can slowly accumulate miles across multiple statement cycles, transfer when you're ready to book, and not feel rushed. There's no expiration clock running against you.

    Sources indicate that finally, the no fuel surcharges policy is a genuine differentiator. Many programs — particularly those involving European carriers — tack on $300–$600 in surcharges that gut your redemption's net value. HawaiianMiles charges no fuel surcharges on Hawaiian-operated flights. Your 7,500 miles covers the flight. Taxes and fees on interisland tickets are minimal, often just a few dollars. What you see is what you get.

    Recent findings suggest that go to hawaiianairlines.com and use the 'Book' tool, selecting 'Reward Travel' as your travel type. Enter your route — for example, HNL to OGG (Honolulu to Kahului, Maui) or HNL to LIH (Honolulu to Lihue, Kauai). Plug in your desired travel date and search. You're looking for economy award space priced at 7,500 miles. Availability on interisland routes is almost always wide open — this is one of the best availability scores (5/5) of any sweet spot in this guide series, but it costs nothing to confirm before you transfer.

    If you don't have a HawaiianMiles account, create one at hawaiianairlines.com — it takes about two minutes and is free. Note your HawaiianMiles number. You'll need it for the transfer step.

    It has been revealed that from Marriott Bonvoy®: Use this only as a last resort due to the 3:1 ratio. Navigate to Bonvoy's transfer portal and select HawaiianMiles. Allow up to 5 days.

    It has been revealed that hawaiianMiles opens its booking window 330 days out. If you're planning a Hawaii trip far in advance and have specific flight times in mind, you can search and book early. That stated, given the excellent availability on these routes, booking 2–4 weeks out is usually fine.

    This is rare for interisland routes, but if it happens, try: searching adjacent dates, looking at different departure times on the same route, or checking alternate routing (e.g., OGG to LIH instead of HNL to LIH directly). Interisland availability doesn't fluctuate the way transatlantic business class does.

    In a recent development, card links may earn ChooseFI a commission. See our advertiser disclosure.

    Sources indicate that let's make this concrete. You're planning a two-week Hawaii trip for two people. You've booked your Honolulu arrival flight separately, and now you need to connect the dots between islands: Honolulu (HNL) to Kahului, Maui (OGG) mid-trip, and then Maui (OGG) to Lihue, Kauai (LIH) before heading home.

    The cash price check: Pull up hawaiianairlines.com and look at what these tickets retail for. On a typical mid-trip travel day, the HNL→OGG segment is priced at $189 per person. The OGG→LIH hop runs $149 per person. For two travelers, that's $676 in cash — before you've bought a single plate of shave ice.

    Industry observers note that the points price: Each segment costs 7,500 HawaiianMiles per person in economy. Two passengers, two flights: 30,000 HawaiianMiles total, plus roughly $10–$20 in taxes and fees across both bookings. No fuel surcharges.

    The CPP calculation: You're replacing $676 in cash spending with 30,000 miles. That's 2.25 cents per point — well above the 0.8–1.2 cpp you'd expect on typical HawaiianMiles redemptions, and solidly within the 1.3–3.3 cpp sweet spot range for this redemption.

    Sources indicate that what the experience looks like: Hawaiian's interisland product is no-frills — these are 20-to-40-minute flights on Boeing 717s. You won't get a meal or premium service. But you will get a reliable, on-time carrier, clean aircraft, and the undeniable satisfaction of hopping between two of the most beautiful island destinations on Earth without opening your wallet at the gate.

    Recent findings suggest that for the ChooseFI traveler, the win isn't the in-flight experience — it's the mental accounting shift. You budgeted for interisland flights; now that budget goes to a sunset sailing charter or a snorkeling excursion instead. The points paid for the planes. The cash funds the memories.

    According to recent reports, do: Transfer Points in the Right Batch Size HawaiianMiles doesn't allow you to transfer partial miles back out, so calculate exactly how many you need before initiating a transfer. For two passengers on two flights, that's 30,000 miles. Transfer exactly that amount — or a small buffer — rather than dumping your entire MR balance into a program you may not use frequently.

    It has been revealed that do: Use Amex MR or Bilt as Your Primary Earning Strategy Since HawaiianMiles are earned primarily through flying, your accumulation plan should center on transferable currencies. The Amex Gold Card (4x on dining and groceries) and Amex Platinum (5x on flights) are elite MR earners. Bilt's no-annual-fee card earning on rent is underused by the ChooseFI community for exactly this kind of transfer.

    Do: Search for Availability Before You Transfer This is worth repeating as a pro tip because newly introduced points travelers make this mistake constantly. Transfer speeds are 1–2 days for Amex MR and Bilt. Don't transfer points and then discover the flight you wanted is sold out. Always confirm availability first, then transfer, then book immediately once miles land.

    In a recent development, avoid: Using Marriott Bonvoy® for This Transfer At a 3:1 ratio, you'd spend 22,500 Bonvoy points for a 7,500-mile award. Bonvoy points are worth approximately 0.7–0.9 cpp on their own best redemptions. The math doesn't hold here — save your Bonvoy points for hotel redemptions.

    It has been revealed that do: Consider the Merger Context Hawaiian Airlines is in the process of merging with Alaska Airlines, and HawaiianMiles may eventually transition into Alaska Mileage Proposal. Pay attention to program announcements. This could change transfer partners, award pricing, or program structure. The current sweet spot exists now — book it while the program operates under its current rules.

    In a recent development, avoid: Waiting for a 'Better' Redemption on These Miles HawaiianMiles are a limited-use currency. They're excellent for interisland and mainland-to-Hawaii flights, but they don't transfer to other airlines and don't unlock international business class sweet spots. If you've got miles in this program, use them for exactly what they're designed for — Hawaiian flights — rather than letting them sit hoping for a better opportunity that may never come.

    Recent findings suggest that do: Book Multiple Segments in a Single Trip If you're doing a true multi-island itinerary, every interisland hop is 7,500 miles. Three islands means two hops — 15,000 miles per person. Plan your island sequence to minimize backtracking, and book all segments at once once your miles transfer.

    Make multi-island trips affordable with the right points strategy.

    Major Hawaiian Islands Connected.
