    Industry observers note that most visitors to Hawaii stick to one island because interisland flights add $100-$400+ per person to the trip cost. By using points for these short hops, you unlock a fundamentally different Hawaii experience — island-hopping from Oahu to Maui to the Massive Island to Kauai without the airfare costs stacking up. This is a multiplier strategy: you are not just saving on one flight, you are enabling an entirely different type of trip. Combining a points-funded mainland-to-Hawaii flight with points-funded interisland hops creates a nearly free (in cash) multi-island Hawaiian vacation.

    In a recent development, decide which islands you want to visit and in what order. The most common combinations are Oahu + Maui, Oahu + Major Island, or a three-island itinerary. Map out how many interisland hops you need so you know the total points required.

    Recent findings suggest that check Hawaiian Airlines (7,500 miles each way), Southwest (variable, typically 4,000-8,000 points), and United (5,000-7,500 miles) for each interisland segment. Southwest often offers the best flexibility with no change fees and no blackout dates.

    For Hawaiian Airlines, transfer Amex Membership Rewards. For Southwest, earn Rapid Rewards directly or transfer from Chase (transfer to Southwest is currently limited). For United segments, transfer from Chase or use Turkish Miles&Smiles for even lower pricing.

    In a recent development, book each interisland hop as a separate one-way award. This gives you maximum flexibility to mix airlines and optimize pricing per segment. One-way awards have no penalty compared to round trips on these short routes.

    In a recent development, align your interisland hops with your arrival and departure flights. Arrive on one island and depart from a different one (open-jaw booking) to avoid backtracking. For example, arrive Honolulu, hop to Maui, depart Maui to the mainland.

    It has been revealed that hawaiian Airlines has the most extensive interisland network and offers the most daily frequencies. Southwest Airlines also operates key interisland routes (Honolulu-Maui, Honolulu-Kona, Honolulu-Lihue). United flies select interisland segments as well. Each airline has different award pricing and transfer partner access.

    According to recent reports, hawaiian Airlines interisland awards typically price at 7,500 HawaiianMiles each way. Southwest varies by cash fare but generally costs 4,000-8,000 Rapid Rewards points each way for interisland hops. United interisland segments can be booked for 5,000-7,500 miles using various Star Alliance partner programs.

    Yes, especially when booking multiple hops. A family of four making two interisland hops at $150 each way would spend $1,200 in cash. Converting that to points frees up significant cash for accommodations, activities, and dining. The per-point value (1.5-2.5 cents) is reasonable, and the trip flexibility gained is substantial.

    A popular strategy is to fly into Honolulu (Oahu), hop to Maui for beaches and Haleakala, then continue to the Big Island (Kona) for volcanoes and snorkeling, and optionally finish on Kauai for dramatic scenery. Each hop is 30-60 minutes. Allow 2-3 days minimum per island.

    According to recent reports, this redemption was built for families and couples planning a multi-island Hawaii vacation — full stop. If you're visiting multiple islands (which most Hawaii first-timers and repeat visitors do), you're already mentally budgeting for interisland flights. This sweet spot simply redirects that cash budget back into your pocket and replaces it with points.

    In a recent development, families get a 5/5 Family Friendly score here for good reason: availability is wide open, booking is simple, and the economics scale beautifully. Four people, two hops = 60,000 miles to cover potentially $1,200+ in interisland airfare. That's an extraordinary displacement of vacation cash.

    Beginners are explicitly welcomed by this redemption's design. There's no partner airline complexity, no fuel surcharge math to calculate, no routing rules to decode. You search on Hawaiian's website, you transfer points, you book. The 5/5 Beginner Friendly and Easy to Book scores reflect that this is genuinely one of the simplest award redemptions you can execute.

    Minimum points needed: 7,500 HawaiianMiles per person per segment. For a solo traveler doing two hops, that's 15,000 miles. For a family of four doing two hops, that's 60,000 miles.

    Recent findings suggest that this is NOT for: Travelers who don't have an Amex MR or Bilt account and no path to earning HawaiianMiles rapidly. It's also not ideal for travelers who only need a single interisland flight — the opportunity cost of setting up the transfer relationship for 7,500 miles may not be worth it unless you're already accumulating MR points for other redemptions.

    This redemption earns a **Beginner** rating — and it genuinely deserves it. In a world of waitlists, fuel surcharges, routing rules, and phone-only bookings, Hawaiian interisland awards are refreshingly clean. **What makes it easy:** Award availability is consistently excellent (5/5). The booking portal is functional and user-friendly. There are no fuel surcharges to calculate. Miles never expire, so there's no pressure. You can complete the entire redemption — from transfer initiation to confirmed booking — in about 48 hours. **The one genuine friction point:** Earning HawaiianMiles isn't as straightforward as earning Chase Ultimate Rewards or Amex MR. Hawaiian doesn't have a widely-used co-branded credit card for most people's everyday spend. This means you're dependent on transfer partners, and the Amex MR and Bilt paths are your primary options. If you don't have either, this redemption becomes harder to access. **Tip 1:** Start with an Amex card that earns Membership Rewards — the Amex Gold is the ChooseFI community favorite for everyday earning. Once you're accumulating MR points, you have a direct path to Hawaiian via a 1:1 transfer. **Tip 2:** Always search award availability before transferring. It takes 30 seconds and protects you from the one mistake that could derail an otherwise smooth booking. **Tip 3:** Don't overthink the merger situation. Hawaiian and Alaska remain separate programs today. Book what's in front of you. If you can earn Amex MR points, you can execute this redemption. It's the perfect first award booking for a ChooseFI member who wants to see how the system works without risking complexity.

    According to recent reports, this sweet spot was last verified over 90 days ago. Award availability and pricing may have changed — verify current rates before booking.

    Recent findings suggest that interisland awards are the key that unlocks multi-island Hawaii vacations without the stacking airfare costs that keep most travelers on a single island. At 7,500-10,000 miles per hop, the points cost is modest, and the trip transformation is significant. Whether you use Hawaiian Airlines miles, Southwest Rapid Rewards, or United partner programs, the strategy is the same: let points handle the short hops so your cash stays in your pocket for experiences. Combined with a points-funded mainland-to-Hawaii flight, interisland awards make a multi-island Hawaiian vacation one of the most achievable aspirational trips in travel rewards.

That's the emotional core of this sweet spot, and it's one of the most powerful entry points into travel rewards for the ChooseFI community. Rent is typically your single largest monthly expense, and for years it was a dead end — money out the door with zero return. Bilt Rewards changed that equation entirely. Here's the math that should stop you mid-scroll: a single night at a Category 4 Hyatt — think Hyatt Place in a major city or a solid Park Hyatt property in a secondary market — costs around $150–$250 in cash. With World of Hyatt points, that same night runs 15,000 points. Transfer your Bilt points at a 1:1 ratio, and you've just redeemed at roughly 1–1.7 cents per point at the low end. But at a Category 6 or 7 property — a Grand Hyatt in Tokyo, a Alila in Bali, an Andaz on the Sunset Strip — cash rates climb to $350–$600 per night while the award chart holds steady. That's where you hit **4–8 cents per point**, the upper end of what any hotel currency in the world delivers. The CPP range for this redemption runs **2–8 cents per point**, with a retail value of **$100–$400 per redemption unit**. In loyalty currency terms, that's elite-tier performance. Most hotel points deliver 0.5–0.8 cents. Hyatt points, earned through your rent payment and transferred instantly, routinely deliver 3–5x that value. This is a **pricing inefficiency built into Hyatt's fixed award chart**. Hyatt hasn't aggressively devalued the way other programs have. The chart still prices aspirational properties at points levels that don't reflect their true cash cost — and Bilt gives you a direct pipeline to those points through the expense you can't avoid. For anyone on the path to FI, that's not a hack. That's just math working in your favor.

    Why rent-to-hotel is one of the most accessible travel rewards sweet spots.

    The core insight here has two parts, and understanding both will change how you think about every dollar of rent you pay going forward.

    Part One: Bilt Is the Only Card That Earns Points on Rent With No Fee.

    Industry observers note that most landlords don't accept credit cards. Those that do typically charge a 2–3% processing fee, which instantly erases any rewards value. Bilt solved this by partnering directly with property management companies and creating a system where you pay rent via the Bilt app, and the payment processes as ACH (no fee to you or your landlord), while Bilt credits your account with points. You earn 1x point per dollar on rent, up to 100,000 points per year. On a $2,000/month rent payment, that's 24,000 Hyatt points annually from a bill you were paying anyway. Zero incremental spend. Zero fees.

    Recent findings suggest that the one rule to know: you must make at least 5 transactions on your Bilt card each statement period to earn points on rent. Five purchases — even five $1 transactions — unlocks the rent earnings. This is a simple, low-lift requirement.

    Part Two: World of Hyatt's Fixed Award Chart Is the Unlock.

    Once your Bilt points are sitting in your account, you transfer them to World of Hyatt at a 1:1 ratio, and the transfer is instant. No waiting 3–5 business days. No points in limbo while availability disappears. You search, you find availability, you transfer, you book — in a single session if you want.

    Hyatt's award chart is category-based, fixed pricing from 3,500 points (Category 1) to 45,000 points (Category 8) per night. This is the inefficiency. When a Park Hyatt in a major international city costs $500 in cash but only 30,000 points (Category 6), you're extracting 1.67 cents per point at minimum — and in peak season when cash rates hit $700, you're at 2.3+ cpp. The chart doesn't move with cash prices.

    Do: Stack Hyatt's 5th Night Free Benefit.

    World of Hyatt awards include a fifth-night-free benefit on standard award redemptions when you book five or more consecutive nights. On a five-night stay at a Category 5 property (20,000 points/night), you'd normally pay 100,000 points — but with the fifth night free, it's 80,000 points for five nights. That's a 20% improvement in value with zero extra effort. Plan longer trips to unlock this.

    Do: Book 395 Days Out for Peak Destinations.

    Hyatt opens award inventory at the same time as cash inventory — 395 days in advance. For high-demand properties (think Park Hyatt Maldives at Hadahaa or Alila Ventana Big Sur), availability at standard rates disappears rapidly. Set a calendar reminder and search early.

    Avoid: Transferring Points Before Confirming Availability.

    Bilt-to-Hyatt transfers are instant and irreversible. If you transfer 30,000 points and then can't find the availability you thought you saw, those points are now in Hyatt — and if you don't use them, they expire after 24 months of account inactivity. Always search Hyatt first, confirm dates and property, then transfer.

    Avoid: Missing the 5-Transaction Monthly Minimum.

    It has been revealed that this is the most common Bilt mistake. If you forget to make five purchases on your Bilt card in a given month, you earn zero points on rent — not reduced points, zero. Automate five small recurring charges to the card and never think about it again.

    Do: Target Category 4–6 Properties for Best Value.

    Sources indicate that ## The Moment You Recline Into ANA "The Room" The flight attendant slides your suite door closed. You're somewhere over the Pacific, 35,000 feet above the ocean, enclosed in what ANA calls "The Room" — a fully private, floor-to-ceiling enclosed business class suite on a Boeing 777-300ER. The seat converts to a fully flat 78-inch bed. There's direct aisle access. The service is famously meticulous. And you're flying from New York to Tokyo in a product that rivals first class on most other carriers. This is not a fantasy. This is what 90,000 Virgin Atlantic Flying Club miles buys you on ANA's JFK → NRT route. ### The Math That Should Stop You Cold A one-way business class ticket on ANA between New York and Tokyo typically retails for **$6,000 to $12,000 in cash**. That's not a typo. Premium cabin trans-Pacific fares are genuinely that expensive, which is precisely why the ChooseFI community treats travel rewards as a core pillar of the FI lifestyle — you're unlocking experiences that would otherwise require years of extra saving. At 90,000 Virgin Atlantic miles for that same seat, your points are delivering **6.7 to 13.3 cents per point (CPP)** in value. To put that in context: most points are considered "good" redemptions at 1.5–2 CPP. This redemption is 4 to 9 times that benchmark. This is what a true sweet spot looks like. ### Why the Gap Exists Virgin Atlantic prices its ANA partner awards using a **fixed award chart** — a relic of the old loyalty program era when airlines published static pricing tables rather than dynamic, revenue-based pricing. ANA's own Mileage Club program charges 75,000–90,000 miles for the same route. Virgin Atlantic's chart prices it at 90,000, but — and here's the critical part — **with zero fuel surcharges on partner-operated flights**. What you see is what you pay. The result is one of the most compelling premium cabin redemptions in all of loyalty programs. The ChooseFI community's founding principle is that every dollar has a job. When 90,000 transferable points can do the job of $12,000 in cash, that's not just travel rewards — that's an asymmetric opportunity you'd be leaving on the table.

    A group of elderly residents at a retirement home in France have been introduced GTA 6, and some are already hoping to get their hands on the game for Christmas.

    Rockstar Games’ highly anticipated Grand Theft Auto 6 finally debuted on November 19, 2026, more than 13 years after the release of GTA 5.

    The open-world crime game has attracted enormous attention worldwide, with fans taking time off work to play it. According to French broadcaster TF1, requests for annual leave in France increased by 8% around the game’s launch. Now, the game has been introduced to the older generations.

    On November 20, residents at the Domitys senior living facility in Serris, Seine-et-Marne, were introduced to GTA 6 as part of an organized gaming session.

    As reported by ICI Paris Île-de-France, the residents swapped their usual activities for an opportunity to explore the game’s virtual world, with many particularly enjoying its boat-driving sequences.

    It has been revealed that 82-year-old Jacqueline was among the most enthusiastic participants, successfully collecting two packages of cocaine during a mission. “I had never touched a controller before 9am this morning. And by 2:30pm, I was fishing out two packages of drugs,” she joked.

    Another resident, 86-year-old Lucienne, was equally impressed by the game’s visuals, describing them as incredible and comparing the experience to watching a real film.

    Meanwhile, 75-year-old Yvan admitted that the controls were difficult to master, joking that he was no longer 20 and struggled to keep up with the action.

    Staff explained that the residents had found driving and shooting particularly challenging, but enjoyed exploring the environment by boat.

    The experience proved popular enough that Lucienne noted she intended to ask her children for GTA 6 for Christmas, while Jacqueline suggested installing a console in the communal lounge.

    Players have found that music in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+’s fresh GTA 6-themed secret run was made with Suno, as the free DLC sits at Overwhelmingly Negative recent reviews on Steam.

    Creator Edmund McMillen has since noted he had no idea the music was AI-generated, with publisher Nicalis now patching it out of the game.

    The run arrived in the same patch that brought Repentance+ to PS5, Xbox, and Switch 2 on November 19, a release date publisher Nicalis picked to go head-to-head with GTA 6.

    Entering the seed V1CE BSMT unlocks a Vice City-inspired daily run with its own soundtrack, made up of seven songs plus a handful of intros and outros.

    A player on the Binding of Isaac subreddit extracted the run’s music from the game files and found several tracks still carrying metadata reading “made with suno,” along with links to the songs on Suno’s site.

    The metadata on one track indicates it was created on October 30, 2026, less than three weeks before the update went live. Other players have since checked the files and confirmed the find.

    According to recent reports, the run itself is credited to a modder known as Mr. Headcrab, who the original poster claims is “staunchly anti-AI” and had no idea the music was generated.

    Valve requires developers to disclose AI-generated content on a game’s Steam page, but Repentance+’s store listing makes no mention of it.

    The DLC currently sits at Overwhelmingly Negative recent reviews, with only 10% of 908 reviews from the past 30 days positive, though the same update has also been blamed for breaking mods and causing crashes.

    Recent findings suggest that the community-run Isaac wiki has since added a note flagging the AI-generated tracks. Nicalis has yet to comment on the music or add a disclosure to the Steam page.

    McMillen addressed the backlash on X, making it clear the music had been added without his knowledge.

    “Woke up to a sh*t show, obviously I had no idea it featured generated music in the daily run,” he wrote. “Looking into how that happened and getting it removed, stay tuned.”.

    Woke up to a shit show, obviously I had no idea it featured generated music in the daily run, looking into how that happened and getting it removed, stay tuned.

A JAL Business Class ticket from Seattle (SEA) to Tokyo Narita (NRT) typically retails between **$5,000 and $10,000** in cash. That's a real number — pull up JAL.com on any given date and you'll see it. Yet Alaska Mileage Strategy prices this exact award at just **60,000 miles** one way. On a $5,000 ticket, that's **8.3 cents per point**. On a $10,000 ticket — which is common during peak travel periods — that's a staggering **16.7 cents per point**. The ChooseFI benchmark for a "good" redemption is typically 1.5 to 2 cents per point. This blows past that by a factor of five to ten. Why does this gap exist? Because Alaska Mileage Plan uses a **fixed award chart** to price partner redemptions. They set the JAL Business Class rate years ago and haven't moved it in step with rising cash fares. As international business class prices have climbed, the points cost has stayed anchored — and that's the pricing inefficiency that savvy travelers exploit. This isn't a loophole that disappears tomorrow. JAL and Alaska have a deep, long-standing partnership. Alaska has consistently maintained this pricing as one of the crown jewels of its partner award chart. For anyone building toward financial independence who also wants to see the world in comfort, this redemption represents exactly what the FI travel rewards philosophy is about: using the system's own rules to access experiences that cash-wealthy people pay enormous sums for, nearly free.

    A sweet spot that punches far above its weight in cents-per-mile value.

    The mechanism behind this sweet spot is elegantly simple once you see it, and understanding it will help you recognize similar opportunities across the loyalty landscape.

    Alaska's Fixed Award Chart Is the Key.

    In a recent development, most major airline programs have shifted to dynamic pricing — meaning award costs fluctuate with demand, just like cash prices. Alaska Mileage Plan has largely resisted this for its partner awards. JAL Business Class from North America is priced at a flat 60,000 Alaska miles one way, period. It doesn't matter if it's Golden Week in Japan or a random Tuesday in February. The chart price holds.

    Recent findings suggest that this creates an extraordinary opportunity because JAL cash fares are not fixed. They respond to demand, fuel costs, seasonality, and competitive dynamics. When those fares rise — as they have substantially in recent years — your 60,000 miles buy proportionally more value. The inefficiency widens the more expensive the cash fare becomes.

    Here's a detail that separates Alaska from many other programs: Alaska Mileage Strategy charges zero fuel surcharges on any partner award booking. This is significant. Some programs (looking at you, British Airways Avios) pass through carrier-imposed surcharges that can add $400–$800 to a theoretically cheap award. With Alaska, your out-of-pocket is taxes only — typically $50–$150 on a transpacific itinerary. Your 60,000-mile redemption costs you 60,000 miles plus roughly $100. Full stop.

    The Transfer Path: Marriott Bonvoy® Is Your On-Ramp.

    Alaska Mileage Plan has no direct credit card transfer partners in the traditional Chase/Amex/Citi sense. This is the most important nuance of this redemption to understand. You cannot transfer Chase Ultimate Rewards or Amex Membership Rewards directly to Alaska. Instead, the primary transfer path runs through Marriott Bonvoy®.

    In a recent development, the ratio is 3 Marriott points to 1 Alaska mile, and transfers typically take 1 to 5 days to complete. There's also the well-known Marriott bonus: transfer 60,000 Marriott points and receive 5,000 bonus miles, meaning 60,000 Marriott points nets you 25,000 Alaska miles. This makes earning Alaska miles via Marriott cards (like the Marriott Bonvoy Boundless or Brilliant) a viable — if not the most efficient — path.

    Recent findings suggest that the more efficient earning strategy for most ChooseFI members is to apply directly for the Alaska Airlines Visa card, which regularly offers strong welcome bonuses, or to fly Alaska-operated flights. Miles in Alaska Mileage Strategy never expire, which means you can accumulate patiently without pressure.

    The Routing Rules Bonus: Free Stopovers.

    Industry observers note that alaska allows a free stopover on one-way awards — a benefit almost no other major US program offers anymore. On a one-way award from the US to Japan, you could stop in Tokyo for several days, then continue to another destination, all for the same 60,000 miles. This is an advanced move that can double the value of a single award ticket.

    Recent findings suggest that book at up to 331 days in advance — Alaska's booking window. For popular travel dates to Japan, searching early is strongly advised.

    Recent findings suggest that before you transfer a single point, confirm the seats exist. Go to jal.com and use JAL's own award search tool. JAL releases excellent Business Class award inventory to partners — this is one of the best-availability premium cabin routes in the game — but you still want to verify before committing.

    Recent findings suggest that search your target dates in "Award Booking" mode. Look for "J" class availability (Business Class). JAL's 787-9 Sky Suite III product operates on the Seattle–Tokyo Narita route, so filter for that routing specifically. Try flexible dates — a day or two of flexibility can reveal significantly more availability. You can search up to 330+ days out, so don't wait until the last minute.

    In a recent development, you need 60,000 Alaska Mileage Initiative miles per one-way Business Class ticket. Check your existing Alaska Mileage Plan balance at alaskaair.com. If you're short, your transfer path is Marriott Bonvoy® at a 3:1 ratio — so 60,000 Alaska miles requires 180,000 Marriott Bonvoy® points (though you'll receive a 5,000-mile bonus when transferring 60,000 Marriott points at a time, so plan accordingly).

    Sources indicate that initiate transfers at marriott.com under "Transfer Points." Build in 1 to 5 days for the transfer to post to your Alaska account. Do not call Alaska to book until the miles are confirmed in your balance.

    Alaska partner awards with JAL must be booked by phone — you cannot book JAL awards on Alaska's website. Call Alaska Mileage Initiative at 1-800-252-7522. Have the following ready:.

    Tell the agent you'd like to book a partner award on JAL using miles. Give them the exact flight number and date. Agents are generally familiar with this redemption — it's a popular one.

If an agent quotes you a surcharge, politely clarify — this is a known Alaska policy. The total cash component should be well under $200.

    If your ideal dates show no availability, try these tactics: search plus or minus three days, look at alternate departure cities (JAL also operates from Los Angeles, Chicago, and New York), or set a calendar reminder to check again — JAL sometimes releases additional inventory closer to departure as business travelers book and cancel. The 331-day booking window means early searchers have the best selection.

    Alaska Airlines is not part of any major airline alliance (Star Alliance, Oneworld, or SkyTeam), which gives it unusual freedom to set its own partner award pricing. While alliance members must coordinate pricing frameworks, Alaska negotiates individual deals with each partner airline. This independence is why Alaska can price JAL business class at 60,000 miles when alliance-member programs charge 70,000-100,000 miles for the same seats. The tradeoff is that Alaska's partner award availability can be more limited than what you would find through an alliance booking, making timing and flexibility critical.

    Let's make this concrete. You and your partner are planning a trip to Japan in the spring — cherry blossom season, the dream itinerary for so many in the ChooseFI community.

    The Points Price: 60,000 Alaska miles per person. For two passengers, that's 120,000 Alaska miles plus approximately $200–$250 in taxes. Total cash outlay: roughly $225 for the pair.

    The CPP: At a conservative $7,000 cash fare, 60,000 miles delivers 11.7 cents per point — nearly six times the standard benchmark for a great redemption.

    You check in at Seattle's dedicated JAL Business Class counter — no line, expedited security. At boarding, you turn left into the 787's Business Class cabin and find your JAL Sky Suite III: a fully enclosed suite with a sliding privacy door, a 43-inch seat that converts to a fully flat 78-inch bed, a 24-inch HD monitor, and dedicated storage. The seat has direct aisle access — you never have to climb over a seatmate.

    Sources indicate that JAL's inflight service is consistently ranked among the best in the world. The meal service features both Western and Japanese options, sake and premium spirits, and attentive crew who seem genuinely delighted to serve you. The 9–10 hour flight to Narita passes in quiet, restful comfort. You arrive refreshed.

    Given Alaska's limited transfer partners, the most reliable path to a large Alaska miles balance is the Alaska Airlines Visa Signature card, which regularly offers welcome bonuses of 40,000–75,000 miles. Stack two cardholders in your household — you and your partner each earn a welcome bonus — and you have a round-trip business class redemption funded almost entirely from sign-up offers.

    Marriott-to-Alaska transfers take 1 to 5 days and are irreversible. Never initiate the transfer until you've confirmed the award space exists on JAL.com. Transferring speculatively and then discovering the seat is gone is a painful and costly mistake.

    While JAL does release excellent inventory — hence the availability score of 4 out of 5 — "year round" availability doesn't mean unlimited. Japanese holidays (Golden Week, Obon in August, New Year's) see compressed availability. The best open inventory is typically September through November and January through mid-February.

    In a recent development, alaska's policy is no fuel surcharges on partner awards, but always verify the final tax-and-fee total before giving your credit card number. Your total out-of-pocket should be well under $200 per ticket. If it's higher, ask the agent to itemize.

    This redemption is built for the ChooseFI couple or solo traveler who has been intentionally accumulating Alaska miles — or Marriott Bonvoy® points — and wants to experience transpacific Business Class without the $8,000 price tag. If Japan is on your bucket list and you're willing to do a phone call to complete the booking, this is one of the highest-value redemptions in the entire loyalty ecosystem.

    Minimum points needed: 60,000 Alaska miles per person. A couple needs 120,000 miles for two one-way Business Class tickets.

    This redemption is rated **moderate** — and that rating is honest. It's not beginner-friendly (rated 2 out of 5 for beginners), but it's absolutely achievable for anyone willing to learn the two-step process. **What makes it moderate:** First, earning Alaska miles is less straightforward than earning Chase Ultimate Rewards or Amex points. Alaska has **no direct credit card transfer partners** in the major bank ecosystems, which means you can't funnel everyday Amex or Chase spend into Alaska miles directly. You're relying on Alaska co-branded credit cards or the Marriott Bonvoy® transfer path. Second, partner award bookings **cannot be completed online** — you must call Alaska Mileage Initiative. For travelers accustomed to booking everything digitally, this feels like friction. In practice, the call takes 15–20 minutes with a prepared agent and is genuinely straightforward. Third, while availability is rated 4 out of 5 (excellent by transpacific standards), you still need to plan ahead, particularly for peak Japan travel seasons. **Three tips to make it easier:** 1. **Start with the Alaska Airlines Visa card** — it's the most direct route to a large Alaska miles balance and regularly offers competitive welcome bonuses. 2. **Do your availability research on JAL.com before calling** — walk into that phone call with the flight number, date, and cabin class already confirmed. The booking becomes a five-minute transaction. 3. **Book 6–10 months out** for peak dates — this eliminates most of the availability stress and gives you time to transfer points if needed. If you've already booked one partner award by phone with any airline, this will feel familiar. If this is your first, the effort is absolutely worth it for a redemption worth 8–17 cents per point.

    A bus driver in Japan has been removed from driving duties after licking the hand straps and handrails inside his bus during a livestream, apparently at the request of a female streamer.

    The driver works for Keikyu Bus, which runs services across Tokyo and Kanagawa, including routes to Haneda Airport, and the incident took place on November 16 after the bus had finished service for the day.

    Footage of the livestream, which spread swiftly on social media, indicates the pair chatting on a split screen, with the streamer directing him to specific parts of the bus.

    “I want you to lick the part you hold onto, a bit further up,” she remarked, according to Japanese outlet coki, to which he replied, “The part you hold?”.

    The streamer has been identified on social media as Riakyun, who reportedly streams on the Japanese livestreaming app Fuwatch, though Keikyu Bus did not mention her in its statement.

    “We sincerely apologize for the great discomfort and concern this has caused,” the manufacturer said, pledging to “thoroughly educate all employees” to prevent it from happening again.

    Keikyu Bus told J-CAST News that the driver has been taken off driving duties, and that it intends to take disciplinary action against him in line with its internal rules.

    The company also confirmed the bus involved has been identified and fully disinfected and cleaned.

    An automated fire detection system at a ski resort in China has gone viral after repeatedly spraying water at a food booth’s sign, leaving viewers convinced it mistook pictures of flames for a real fire.

    Footage of the bizarre incident shows a ceiling-mounted water cannon blasting a barbecue stall’s flame-covered sign as confused onlookers watch.

    The incident occurred on November 19 at Wanlong Ski Resort in Zhangjiakou, Hebei province.

    As shown in footage, the automated system fires a powerful stream of water directly toward a sign decorated with images of burning charcoal.

    The video quickly spread online, with viewers joking that the supposedly intelligent system couldn’t distinguish between a picture of fire and the real thing.

    However, despite the apparent AI blunder, resort officials have offered a different explanation.

    According to Yangtse Evening News, a visitor noted she had ordered lamb skewers shortly before the system activated, with water beginning to spray not long after cooking started.

    Resort officials claimed the system was actually triggered by heat from a charcoal grill positioned behind the sign, rather than mistaking the flame graphics for a genuine blaze.

    In a recent development, staff promptly shut down the equipment and cleaned the affected area, reopening it approximately 20 minutes later. No injuries were reported, and the resort has since adjusted the grill’s position to prevent another incident.

    The footage comes amid growing scrutiny of automated detection systems and their mistakes.

    In October 2025, a teenager was swarmed by armed police after an AI security system mistook a bag of Doritos for a gun.

    More recently, a Pennsylvania high school was forced to scrap its AI security system after ordinary student belongings repeatedly triggered weapon alerts.

    However, now attention has turned to the other joint best-reviewed game of all time: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time.

    The 59-year-old was handed a three-year ban from football matches, while also being forced to pay £500 compensation and a further £600 fine.

That's a pricing inefficiency, and it's one that's been hiding in plain sight for travelers who only know British Airways Avios and never discovered Iberia's **separate, more generous award chart**. The FI mindset is about finding asymmetries — places where the value you receive is wildly disproportionate to what you give up. This is one of the cleanest examples in the entire travel rewards ecosystem. You're not gaming anything. That's the same Avios currency, same points you can transfer from Chase, but priced under Iberia's more favorable structure.

The accounts need to be linked through the Avios household account feature, but it's a powerful tool that many travelers overlook.

Iberia is unusual because it publishes an explicit off-peak calendar with fixed lower pricing during specific date ranges. Off-peak pricing applies to the flight date, not the booking date, so you can book an off-peak flight months in advance and lock in the lower rate. The off-peak discount is roughly 50% compared to peak pricing on the same route. This creates a planning advantage for flexible travelers who can target specific travel windows. Combined with the fact that Avios transfer from five major credit card programs, it is one of the most accessible premium redemptions in the loyalty landscape.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A bird expert who has found every feathery friend in GTA 6 has given his take on the game’s depiction of Leonida’s avian wildlife, praising Rockstar for the detail while also sharing a few notable inaccuracies.

    When you think of GTA 6, taking relaxing cross-country trips in search of local flora and fauna probably isn’t the first thing that comes to mind. Instead, you’re probably keeping an eye out for the best cars to steal, or beefing out Jason and Lucia’s arsenal with deadly weapons for your next massive heist.

    While adrenaline-fueled shootouts and speedy getaways are all part of the game’s fictional Florida, GTA 6’s sunny shores are also home to beautiful wildlife (excluding the terrifying Bigfoot Easter egg).

    One birdwatching enthusiast has ditched the handguns for a pair of binoculars, using his expertise to reveal what Rockstar got right and wrong about GTA 6’s birds.

    Writing in a column for Audubon, birdwatching expert Nicholas Lund shared his experience travelling across Leonida. Lund was particularly taken aback by how much care Rockstar had taken, especially when it comes to the boundaries each bird species has in the game.“The map is true to the ecological boundaries of South Florida, with herons, gulls, and other waterbirds in the south while birds like Red-bellied Woodpecker, Wood Stork, and American Robin are found farther north. Birders know that certain exotic species have made their home in tropical South Florida, including Spot-breasted Oriole and Red Junglefowl, both in the game.”.

    Recent findings suggest that 60 / 60 BIRDS! FOLKS WE DID IT! pic.twitter.com/JVsc4jjlOA.

    Recent findings suggest that so, this means you’ll need to be prepared to grab a car (preferably a fast one), pop on your favorite radio station tunes, and put in the hours driving around Leonida in pursuit of all 60 bird types. It’s not all sweet birdsong, though, as Lund did find a few complications during his quest to spot them all.

    Industry observers note that “I found a number of avian inaccuracies in just my first few hours of playtime. Certain species like Whooping Crane and Red-cockaded Woodpecker are common throughout the map, despite being endangered and threatened, respectively, in real life.

    “Golden Eagles are extremely rare in Florida, but I found one soaring over the Mt. Kalaga area (mountains, one may point out, aren’t found in Florida either),” explained Lund.

    According to recent reports, “Some species have confusing naming quirks. The chickadee is Black-capped instead of Carolina, and there’s a ‘Newly introduced World Oriole’ instead of a Baltimore Oriole, but those changes are likely due to the fact that Carolina and Baltimore don’t exist in the GTA universe.”.

    Rarity and name changes aside, GTA 6’s resident bird watcher was keen to point out that the hunting for birds to document in Rockstar’s open world feels like an accurate representation of Florida-based birdwatching.

    It has been revealed that “There’s garbage almost everywhere, lapping the shorelines and blowing along the streets. There seems to be no inch of landscape in GTA 6 that hasn’t been lessened by the touch of humans. It is, I have to admit, a realistic depiction of birding in South Florida,” he added.

    easily my favorite thing to do so far is just screech to a halt in the middle of a busy intersection and start birding pic.twitter.com/QsDOLmNfYq.

    Lund was also keen to mention that “GTA 6 provides what feels like the most accurate version of modern birding ever put to screen,” while also stating that “obsessing over the realism misses the point of having fun.”.

    As a fan of Rockstar’s recreation, he also urged fellow enthusiasts to visit the real South Florida and see its wildlife for themselves, but noted that GTA 6 has one bonus over the IRL birdwatching experience.

    “Birders can, and should, visit the real South Florida to find the actual birds depicted in the game (and many more), but they can’t do it while also jumping over broken highway bridges on a stolen motorcycle. Birding is a bonus in GTA 6; mayhem is the draw.”.

    You can read the full column on Audubon and follow Nicholas Lund’s Birdist account on X for more birdwatching updates.

    GTA 6 players have found how to stop the trains circulating Leonida, and it’s actually a lot easier than they expected it to be.

    In GTA 5, players spent years trying to bring the train to a halt. They tried everything from blasting it with explosives to parking huge vehicles and planes in its way.

    However, no matter how hard they tried, it would always keep moving forward, laying waste to whoever or whatever was trying to block its path.

    Now that they’ve been let loose in GTA 6, many tried to do the same once again, but they quickly found it’s nowhere near the challenge it once was.

    Industry observers note that in GTA 6, trains behave much more realistically. If you stand on the tracks or block them with a vehicle and give the driver enough time to spot you, they will bring the locomotive to a halt until you move out of the way.

    You can Finally Derail a Moving Train in GTA 6 pic.twitter.com/PQItm03f7e.

    Industry observers note that as you might expect, others have found more dramatic ways to slow it down, such as crashing a dump truck into the front of them. In fact, if you hit one with enough force at the right angle, they can be derailed completely.

    Industry observers note that given how much GTA 6 steps up the realism, it’s probably no surprise that its trains aren’t unstoppable forces of nature. However, while some fans like this approach, others miss the challenge of trying to get a train to stop.

    They nerferd the boss pic.twitter.com/jK8EihWCX6.

    “The nerfed the boss,” wrote one player on X, before adding: “I like the aura farming of GTA 5 train more.”.

    “THE TRAIN LOST IT’S ENTIRE AURA IN GTA 6,” wrote another.

    “Honestly, it feels like they completely stripped the train of any character—GTA 6 visuals are stunning, but the vibe is just missing here,” remarked a third.

    GTA 6’s map is packed full of activities that will no doubt keep players occupied for months, but stopping the train is no longer the puzzle it once was.

    Rockstar Games is reportedly open to selling the movie and television rights to Red Dead Redemption, but Hollywood studios will need a lot more money than Dutch van der Linde ever dreamed of getting his hands on.

    Despite being responsible for some of the most cinematic experiences in gaming, Rockstar has historically been reluctant to let Hollywood adapt its biggest franchises.

    While the studio is reportedly still unwilling to bring Grand Theft Auto to the massive screen, it appears that Arthur Morgan and John Marston could be saddling up for Hollywood.

    According to a report from The Ankler, sources claim Rockstar is now more receptive to the idea of adapting Red Dead Redemption into a movie or television series.

    However, the licensing rights alone could come with a nine-figure price tag.

    “At one point, they were throwing around a purchase price of more than $100 million minimum for licensing rights,” an agent who works with video game writers told the outlet.

    According to recent reports, the news marks a potential change in direction for Rockstar. In 2024, firm co-founder Dan Houser revealed why previous pitches for GTA and Red Dead movies were rejected, citing financial risks and concerns over creative control.

    Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick also expressed caution about adapting its franchises following the disappointing reception to the Borderlands movie.

    There certainly wouldn’t be a shortage of Hollywood stars willing to join the Van der Linde gang, though.

    Jeffrey Dean Morgan, Henry Cavill, and Jack Black have all expressed interest in seeing Red Dead adapted, with Morgan even offering to play Arthur for free.

    Arthur’s original actor, Roger Clark, has also expressed interest in reprising his role in live-action.

    Jeffrey Dean Morgan, Henry Cavill and Jack Black all want a Red Dead Redemption movie.

    Arthur Morgan voice actor says he’s “sure” RDR3 is coming & it could be a much different story.

    Don’t hold your breath for a GTA or Red Dead movie after Take-Two CEO comments.

    Rockstar has yet to publicly confirm its prepares, and no studio has been announced as acquiring the rights. It’s also unclear whether an adaptation would retell the events of either game or explore a completely original story set in the same universe.

    It’s also unclear what effect, if any, this could have on a possible RDR3.

    For now, Red Dead fans will just have to have some goddamn faith that Hollywood can get the money together. Perhaps they’ll turn to GTA 6‘s incredible bank robberies for some inspiration.

    The posts offered no explanation for what would happen when the timer reached zero. That led fans to speculate that Pokemon could finally reveal more about Gen 10, including another look at Winds and Waves, a new Pokemon Presents, or long-requested announcements such as Ruby and Sapphire ports.

It will premiere on the official Pokemon YouTube channel on November 30 at 11 p.m. JST, or 2 p.m. UTC. The “Evergreen” song will then be released digitally on December 1.

    Getting shortlisted for a junior data analyst job depends less on how many courses you have finished and more on what you can show. This strategy breaks preparation into eight skill areas, pairs each one with a learning option and a hands-on task, and gives you a simple test for knowing when to move on.

    Many people preparing for their first analyst role study for months and still struggle to get interviews. Their CVs list SQL, Excel and Tableau, yet nothing on the page shows those tools being used to answer a real question. Recruiters reading dozens of similar applications need something more concrete.

    A course can give your learning a sensible order, but a completion badge states little about how you think. A small analysis that states its question, explains its method and admits its limits tells a hiring manager far more. This initiative aims to collect that kind of proof while you learn, not after.

    In a recent development, start by collecting ten to twenty entry-level postings in the industry you want to join, and tally the tools and tasks they mention. You will swiftly see a pattern. Some roles are built around Excel and routine reporting, while others want SQL, a BI platform and a bit of Python.

    In a recent development, the wider market follows a similar shape. Jobright’s 2026 analysis of data analyst hiring, which looked at 2025–2026 postings from LinkedIn, Indeed and Levels.fyi, found that more than 80% of data analyst jobs mention SQL, over 60% mention Excel or Google Sheets, and roughly half mention Python or R. Let your own tally decide the order you learn in, but expect SQL to sit near the top.

    As you work through each area below, finish with something you can show someone: a query, a tidied dataset, a chart, a one-page report or a portfolio project. Free material is often enough if you can stay disciplined. Pay for teaching only when it gives you something you cannot get alone, such as feedback, accountability or a fixed timetable.

    SQL is how analysts pull, join and summarise records from a database, and a tool like Tableau lets other people explore what you found. Treat them as one workflow rather than two subjects: frame a question, write the query, sanity-check the numbers and present the result so a non-technical reader can follow it.

    In a recent development, SQLBolt offers free, bite-sized SQL lessons that run in the browser, and Tableau publishes free training videos on connecting to data and building dashboards. Used together, they are enough to produce a small end-to-end project.

    If you learn better with a set schedule and an instructor checking your work, you could learn to analyse data with SQL and Tableau from scratch through a guided programme at Heicoders Academy in Singapore. Whichever route you take, compare what is covered, how feedback is given, when sessions run and the full cost against what free resources already offer.

    Proof you can show: A working SQL query set and your first published dashboard.

    Move on when: You can take a question from idea to dashboard on your own, without following a tutorial line by line.

    Spreadsheets are still where much of a team’s day-to-day reporting lives, especially when colleagues don’t write SQL. Get comfortable with filtering, pivot tables, and lookup functions, and learn to spot quiet errors like dates saved as text or one category spelled three different ways.

    The next step is automating the cleanup so it doesn’t have to be repeated by hand each month. Microsoft’s Power Query documentation demonstrates how to import and reshape data in recorded steps that refresh when upcoming data arrives. The same ideas apply in other spreadsheet tools too.

    Proof you can show: A messy export turned into a summary that refreshes itself.

    Move on when: You can clean an untidy CSV and build a report that updates when the source file changes.

    For most junior analyst roles, the technical interview is a SQL test. Basic SELECT statements won’t be enough; interviewers like to probe joins, subqueries, common table expressions and window functions, which answer everyday questions such as running totals or each customer’s first purchase.

    Practise with timed problem sets and review your answers for correctness as well as speed.

    Proof you can show: Confidence going into a live or take-home SQL test.

    Move on when: You can solve intermediate problems in around 15 to 20 minutes each without looking up syntax.

    Recent findings suggest that take-home assignments often come with data that has been made messy on purpose. Reviewers want to see how you deal with missing values, duplicates and inconsistent formats, and whether they can follow your reasoning afterwards.

    Recent findings suggest that keep a short cleaning log as you work, noting each change and why you made it. A separate sheet tab or a list of comments in a notebook both work.

    Proof you can show: A take-home submission a reviewer can audit step by step.

    Move on when: Every change to your dataset is written down with a reason.

    Recent findings suggest that case-study questions test whether you can read numbers sensibly, not just produce them. A working grasp of distributions, means and medians, spread, correlation and sampling will keep you away from the mistakes that undo otherwise good answers, such as quoting an average that a few extreme values have pulled out of shape.

    Proof you can show: Clear, careful answers in case-study interviews.

    Move on when: You can explain in everyday language why two things moving together doesn’t mean one causes the other.

    It has been revealed that every chart should help someone answer a specific question. Learn where bars, lines, scatter plots and simple tables each work best, and how axis ranges, labels and colour can nudge a reader towards the wrong conclusion. On a dashboard, the most notable finding should be the first thing people see.

    Datawrapper’s guidance on picking chart types is a useful free reference. As practice, show the same result in two different chart types and decide which one represents the data more honestly.

    Proof you can show: Portfolio charts that make a point, not just show off features.

    Move on when: A person who has never seen your data can spot the main finding and its caveat at a glance.

    What counts as a useful metric depends on the role. Marketing analysts focus on conversion and retention, operations analysts on delivery times and capacity, and finance analysts on margins and cash flow. Choose one sector and learn exactly how its key measures are defined.

    Proof you can show: A project built around the questions your target industry actually asks.

    Move on when: You can define several sector metrics and describe how a manager would use each one.

    Your portfolio is where the other seven areas come together. Two or three deep, well-documented projects will say more about you than a long list of quick ones. Give each project a README that sets out the question, the data, your method, the findings and the limitations.

    Proof you can show: A portfolio link and a write-up you can talk through in an interview.

    Move on when: Every project clearly explains what it asked, how you answered it and what you found.

    Industry observers note that there is no need to finish all eight areas before you apply. Once you can use the tools your target roles mention, speak honestly about your work and point to two or three clearly explained projects, start sending applications and keep learning alongside them.

    Adjust each application to the job. Lead with a reporting example for spreadsheet-heavy roles, a query that solved a real problem for SQL roles, and a chart that supported a decision for visualisation roles. Be upfront about which work you built independently and which came from guided exercises.

    Do I really need eight courses? No. These are skill areas, not eight required qualifications. A single resource can cover several of them, and practice you do on your own counts as much as classroom learning.

    Is it possible to prepare using only free material? Yes. Free tutorials, open textbooks, official documentation and public datasets cover the fundamentals well. The harder parts are sticking to a routine and finding people who will give you honest feedback.

    In a recent development, which should come first, SQL or spreadsheets? It depends on the jobs you want. Spreadsheets are an easy starting point for reporting roles, while SQL is expected wherever databases are involved. You will want both eventually, so start with whichever your target postings stress most.

    How many portfolio projects should I have? Two or three solid ones are a good start. Each should show a clear question, steps someone else could repeat and an honest reading of the results, rather than several near-identical dashboards.

    Industry observers note that do I need a certificate before I apply? Not usually. Some employers ask for one, but many judge skills through interviews, take-home tasks and tests instead. Go by what each posting actually requires.

    A upcoming Steam game that lets players explore the internet and play minigames together in a single web browser could become your group’s next obsession.

    From viral browser games that allow you to stroke virtual cats to gacha games that let players battle it out in Pokemon card-style battles with Wikipedia pages, 2026 has been a fantastic year for weird and wonderful games.

    Joining this list is INTERNET4, an upcoming Steam game that lets you and your friends fish, compete in general knowledge quizzes, draw, and browse the internet together.

    Browsing the big World Wide Web is usually a solitary thing, but the developers behind INTERNET4 have decided this no longer needs to be the case. Instead, you and eight buddies will be able to team up and explore websites together.

    The main highlight is Wikipedia Challenge, which creates minigames based on information from the popular website and those across the web. You’ll need to follow information between articles to reach the target page, while Research Battle has you investigating a random topic.

    Sources indicate that the latter requires you to show off your answer and even vote amongst your pals to choose the winner. There’s also a more relaxed fishing minigame (who doesn’t like a bit of video game fishing?) where you can catch, record, and compare your bites while surfing the net.

    Sources indicate that tuning into your favorite livestreams and watching videos together is also an option for those who would rather spend their time doomscrolling memes. INTERNET4 also lets you initiative trips by exploring destinations or pull up a game map to discuss strategies between adrenaline-filled gaming sessions.

    Industry observers note that have you ever seen those classic Looney Tunes cartoons where the murderous Wile E. Coyote dashes after the infuriating Road Runner? Usually, a high-speed chase ends with an unexpected comic twist, such as a bundle of dynamite exploding at the wrong time. Perhaps the most famous gag from these iconic animated shorts​​​​​​​ is the one where the plotting Coyote is tricked into running headfirst into a canyon wall painted to look like the entry to a tunnel.

    Some people are at the moment learning that the silly gag can be more convincing than they thought, especially in a video game as hyperrealistic as Grand Theft Auto 6.

    It has been revealed that since the release of Rockstar's open-world game, social media has filled up with clips​​​​​​​ of players running down a street at high speed. Maybe they're in the middle of a police chase, or maybe they're just not paying much attention. The high-speed drive ends in misfortune when the player realizes that the area in front of them isn't a street at all — it's a mural​​​​​​​ that looks like the natural continuation of the street.

    Street art like this is common in GTA 6, but the placement of this particular mural and its muted color palette make it seem like Rockstar fully intended​​​​​​​ for it to mislead people. As such, viral videos showing untimely car crashes have helped popularize the name "Looney Tunes wall" for this part of the game.​​​​​​​ If fans don't call it that, they usually still compare the encounter to Looney Tunes anyway.​​​​​​​.

    The ragebaiting fake wall is between the Stockyard and Decor District in Vice City, at this specific marker:.

    Though it can be infuriating in the heat of the moment,​​​​​​​ fans are delighted by the jest as well. "I really hope they release some stats on how many people hit this wall," one YouTube caption reads.

    According to recent reports, other GTA 6 fans can't believe something so simple got them. To be fair, the area is full of shops — including some spots Jason and Lucia can rob. It's easy to stop looking closely when you're actively trying to run away with a stolen stash as the police chase you. It's also positioned so the surrounding stoplights frame the fake tunnel, adding a physical layer of legitimacy to the optical illusion.

    If you still think you'd never fall for it, don't be too sure.​​​​​​​ Earlier in 2026, a man in Scotland crashed his car into a wall after mistaking a mural featuring two giant eyes for an actual tunnel.​​​​​​​.

    "Bro fell for literally the oldest trick in a book," reads one comment on Reddit in a thread where a player expresses disbelief over the joke.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

    Weekly. Free. One click to leave.

    Sources indicate that 7 Day Free Trial. Cancel Anytime.

    In a recent development, A self-hosted LLM gateway sits between your app and the model provider, so every call pays for one extra hop. We measured that cost for three open-source gateways: the Langfuse AI Gateway, the LiteLLM proxy and AcruxCore. Each one ran on the same machine, in front of the same OpenAI model. LiteLLM added 61 to 67 ms to every non-streaming call. AcruxCore added 15 to 24 ms. Langfuse's number could not be told apart from zero.

    Industry observers note that the bigger lesson was about the measurement itself. Before we controlled for it, one OpenAI network address moved our results by more than any gateway did.

    In a recent development, each number is the median time a gateway added to a direct OpenAI call, with its 95% interval in brackets. A gateway can log each call, and logging takes time, so we ran the test three times with three logging levels.

    The direct call took 781 to 831 ms at the median, so even LiteLLM's cost is under 9% of a short call. Read the tables this way:.

    Industry observers note that the obvious test is to time 100 calls through the gateway, time 100 direct calls, and compare the two medians. That test gives the wrong answer, for two reasons.

    The first reason is noise. OpenAI's own response time moved by hundreds of milliseconds between calls in our runs. The direct call's p95 was 1,047 to 1,233 ms against a median near 800 ms. A gateway that adds 20 ms is hidden inside that spread unless the test removes it.

    It has been revealed that the second reason is the network path to OpenAI. It does not stay the same between a direct client and a gateway, and that difference can be larger than the gateway itself.

    api.openai.com resolves to more than one address. From our network, DNS returned two Cloudflare addresses, and one was much farther away than the other. We measured both with a script that pins one address at a time:.

    On a connection that is already open, both addresses answer in the same time. On a fresh connection, the far address adds about 250 ms, because the TCP and TLS handshakes take that much longer.

    A gateway keeps its connection to OpenAI open between calls. It pays the setup once and then stays on whichever address it reached first. A client that opens a newly introduced connection for each call pays the setup again on every call. How much it pays depends on which address DNS returns that time.

    Node's built-in fetch closes an idle connection after about 4 seconds. So a test client that calls OpenAI every few seconds reconnects on almost every call. In our first, uncontrolled run, the Langfuse gateway came out 43 ms faster than calling OpenAI directly. A gateway cannot be faster than the call it forwards. The direct client paid for new connections, and the gateway did not.

    It has been revealed that the fix has two parts. First, pin api.openai.com to one address on every path. In Docker, that is an extra_hosts entry on each gateway container:.

    Second, let the direct client keep its connection open, as a gateway does. With undici, the HTTP client behind Node's fetch, that is a custom Agent:.

    We then listed each container's open connections to confirm that every path used the same address. The edge-check script is in the repository linked at the end, and it takes about a minute to run from your own network.

    This advice also applies outside benchmarks. If your app calls OpenAI directly from Node, keep the connection open between calls. Otherwise some of your calls pay the handshake, and on a far address that costs about 250 ms.

    Industry observers note that each test sent 150 rounds after 5 warm-up rounds. One round calls OpenAI directly and through each gateway, once without streaming and once with streaming. The order rotates every round, so no path always goes first or last.

    Sources indicate that for each round, the script takes the gateway's time minus the direct call's time in that same round. Calls in one round are made within a few seconds of each other, so a slow moment at OpenAI hits all four paths together and cancels out of the difference. The script then reports the median of the 150 differences.

    Industry observers note that the interval comes from a bootstrap. The script draws 150 differences at random, with replacement, and takes their median. It repeats that 2,000 times, and the middle 95% of those medians is the interval. This is a shortened version of the script's function:.

    In a recent development, an interval that includes zero means the test could not separate the gateway's cost from zero. That is what the Langfuse rows show. It does not prove that the cost is zero.

    Every call used OpenAI gpt-6-luna with reasoning_effort: "none", the same short prompt and a cap of 5 output tokens. A short answer keeps the model's own time small, so more of the measured time belongs to the path. Each streamed call measured the time to its first token. Each non-streamed call measured the time to the full response.

    All three gateways did real work on every call, which made the comparison fair:.

    The three logging levels mapped to these settings:.

    The machine was an AMD Ryzen 9 5900X with 62 GB of RAM, running Fedora Linux and Docker 29.9. All three stacks ran on it at once, and the test was run on 10 November 2026.

    LiteLLM added 61 to 67 ms to the full response, but only 9 to 43 ms to the first streamed token. The first token arrives as soon as the model starts to answer, so time spent before that point reveals up in both numbers. The larger cost without streaming suggests that most of LiteLLM's extra time is spent after the model has answered. We did not profile LiteLLM to confirm this.

    Logging level made no clear difference for any gateway. Adding LiteLLM's Langfuse callback did not raise its cost. AcruxCore's median rose from 15 ms with logging off to 24 ms with full logging, but its intervals overlap across all three runs. AcruxCore's median is 16 to 24 ms above Langfuse's, and those intervals overlap too, so this test does not rank the two of them.

    If 60 ms per call matters to you, as in a chat app that makes several model calls per user message, LiteLLM's cost is real and repeatable. Langfuse and AcruxCore stayed near or within the noise. If your calls take several seconds, any of the three costs less than OpenAI's own variation from one call to the next.

    Before you trust a gateway number, your own or anyone else's, check two things. Was each gateway compared with a direct call in the same round? And did the direct client keep its connection open on the same OpenAI address as the gateway? Without both, the result measures the network path and not the gateway.

    The scripts, Compose files and raw results are on GitHub: scripts/comparison/langfuse-gateway-vs-litellm-vs-acruxcore.

    Talha Anwar is a senior AI and full-stack engineer and writes about building and running AI systems.

    A Latest Jersey pizzeria has been bombarded with death threats, fake orders and one-star reviews after an online mob confused it with another restaurant at the center of a viral feud.

    Electronics repair shop owner Leone Mastrolia, better known on social media as Digital Doctor, found himself embroiled in a dispute with the owner of Nick’s Pizza, located in the same shopping complex as his business in Manahawkin.

    Sources indicate that the drama began when a customer offered to buy Mastrolia lunch. The content creator declined pizza from the neighboring restaurant, citing ongoing complications with his landlord.

    The pizzeria’s owner subsequently contacted police, accusing Mastrolia of harassment after the restaurant began receiving negative reviews.

    A post shared by Digital Doctor Repairs (@digitaldoctorrepairs).

    Mastrolia filmed his interaction with police and uploaded it to social media, with the viral video amassing over 3.1 million views in less than a day.

    However, some viewers looking to retaliate against the restaurant ended up targeting an entirely unrelated business.

    A post shared by Digital Doctor Repairs (@digitaldoctorrepairs).

    Nick’s Pizza and Pasta in Cinnaminson, located more than an hour away from the restaurant involved in the dispute, received upwards of 60 one-star reviews in a single day.

    According to Fresh Jersey 101.5, trolls accused the restaurant of serving expired food and having infestations of mice and cockroaches.

    In a recent development, things escalated when employees began receiving threatening phone calls. Restaurant owner Nick Lubrano and his wife, Sonia Scotto, stated one caller even threatened to murder their family.

    “I’m gonna kill your family,” the caller reportedly said.

    The restaurant was also inundated with suspicious orders, including one from a California phone number requesting eight large pepperoni pizzas.

    Restaurant hits out at “miserable and entitled” diners after viral outrage over tips rule.

    Pizza restaurant faces backlash after confronting 5-year-old’s birthday party for bringing cake.

    Internet rallies behind Red Baron worker who snapped at Instagram prankster.

    The couple eventually learned what had happened after someone spotted the viral videos and contacted them about the mix-up.

    Fortunately, Mastrolia took it upon himself to make things right. In a follow-up video, the repair shop owner visited the pizzeria, apologized in person and handed over $1,000, suggesting the money be used to give away free pizzas or reward employees.

    A post shared by Digital Doctor Repairs (@digitaldoctorrepairs).

    He also urged his followers to stop leaving negative reviews for businesses they had never visited, regardless of whether they had found the right restaurant.

    “Thanks Leo for driving up and personally apologizing to us on behalf of your followers,” Nick’s replied. “Demonstrates your integrity and we respect that a lot!”.

    Meanwhile, longtime customers rallied behind the family-owned pizzeria, which has been operating in Cinnaminson for 14 years, leaving positive reviews and messages of support to counter the online backlash.

    Disney’s Unwatchable Newly introduced Fantasy Movie is a Sloppy Harry Potter-The Incredibles Mash-Up

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (784 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Polygon

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Hexed directors Fawn Veerasunthorn and Jason Hand really want to remind viewers of Disney's most magical movies.
    • Hexed kicks off with a standard exposition dump explaining that Hexe was formed as a sanctuary for persecuted witches and wizards.
    • In a recent development, the story plays out like a chaotic mashup of classic Disney princess tropes, Harry Potter, and The Incredibles.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Hexed directors Fawn Veerasunthorn and Jason Hand really want to remind viewers of Disney's most magical movies. The fantastical realm of Hexe is filled with enchanted objects straight out of Beauty and the Beast. A parody of The Little Mermaid’s sea witch Ursula voiced by Jodi Benson, the star of the 1989 classic, hawks spells in the town square. The three-eyed cat Beef Roger Crummchuk (Walton Goggins) collects figurines, including the one sporting the hat Mickey Mouse wore in Fantasia. But rather than feeling like a love letter to Disney’s legacy, these Easter eggs come across as classic reference slop covering up a jumbled mess of a plot that buries some surprisingly dark ideas in cheerful chaos.

    Hexed kicks off with a standard exposition dump explaining that Hexe was formed as a sanctuary for persecuted witches and wizards. Their realm is protected by a magical spell meant to be empowered through a ritual that the extra-special “chosen witch” will complete during an upcoming lunar event. Billie Doe (Hailee Steinfeld) opened a portal to Hexe when she was a baby, and her overprotective mom Alice (Rashida Jones) has been suppressing her daughter’s powers ever since. But when Billie accidentally regains her abilities and travels to Hexe, she runs afoul of its villainous ruler Queen Celeste (Jodie Foster).

    In a recent development, the story plays out like a chaotic mashup of classic Disney princess tropes, Harry Potter, and The Incredibles. There are lots of cute talking animals and pretty outfits perfect for dress-up – Billie makes a crack about needing a costume change before the final confrontation, then magics up a more stylish cloak. The first scene in Hexed is extremely reminiscent of a visit to Harry Potter’s Diagon Alley, packed with whimsical food, swooping owls, and people wandering around in robes and pointed hats. Like Mr. Incredible, Alice’s attempts to keep her family safe have trapped her in a comically dull life selling boxes in suburban Ohio. She and her daughter come to understand each other better while on an adventure to stop a villain who, just like The Incredible's Syndrome, has decided they should control how special people are.

    According to recent reports, hexed is a very pretty movie, using a vibrant neon-colored palette that’s particularly striking in creepier moments like when Celeste’s shapeshifting part-crow minions descend on Billie, or when the teen has to run from a centipede made of eyeballs. But screenwriters Jared Bush and Dana Ledoux Miller don’t seem to have a coherent reason to drive Billie to each new location for the next chaotic fight. At one point, Billie hits a dead end in her search for answers about the moon ritual and a passing kid just shouts at her that pirates have captured an owl who has the information she needs. How does he know this? How does the owl (voiced by Henry Winkler) know this? Why did the pirates want an owl? None of this is answered.

    In yet another cinematic reference, Billie reveals she just needs to find her own version of the Yellow Brick Road to round up allies to fight the wicked witch. But unlike Dorothy’s friends, Billie’s followers don’t really want anything or have much personality beyond being voiced by notable actors. No one has to make a really difficult decision, and one moment that seems like a dramatic sacrifice is immediately undone for laughs.

    Recent findings suggest that the incoherent plot might have been forgivable if Hexed did a better job at realizing its emotional core. A pair of scenes where Billie and her mom get inside each other’s heads are squandered by mostly repeating moments that already happened in the film, rather than actually showing each other or the audience anything fresh. The reason Alice kept Billie away from Hexe turns out to be a genuinely horrifying dark secret, but rather than really dealing with the fallout from that revelation, the film just switches Alice into cool mom mode. The story immediately moves past the trauma that shaped her parenting style and effectively declares Billie was right about everything.

    The Super Mario Galaxy Movie was also manic, shiny, reference slop, and it made $1 billion. Hexed is unlikely to be that successful, but it leaves open plenty of possibilities for future adventures for kids who want pretty traditional stories of evil queens, good chosen ones, and grateful peasants. Hexed hints at a deeper, darker film that had something more to say about how mothers treat their daughters, but instead it just winds up being a sparkly way of repackaging concepts from more magical movies that came before.

    According to recent reports, hexed premieres in theaters on Nov. 25.

    It has been revealed that not sure if you’ve heard, but the biggest video game of all time is out today: buying Anthropic stock. Yes, in case you haven’t already blown all of your money on the GTA VI Ultimate Edition, you can try your luck at buying one of the most anticipated IPOs of all time when ANT goes public on the Nasdaq later today.

    But you’re likely up, playing the game that is, according to Metacritic, already among the best of all time. It’s presently sitting at a near-perfect 99/100 on the aggregator, with reviewers calling it “a masterpiece” and “gaming’s… greatest love story.” It’s a game in which you can do basically anything you want, from the violent to the vacuous.

    More than anything, though, I’m just excited to discover all the different ways the game allows you to find and consume coffee.

    In a recent development, as I’m sure happened in every newsroom, the conversation this week turned to whether traffic will meaningfully decline today as up to 1.5 million people “call in sick” to play GTA VI. If you’ve been awake since the crack of dawn trying to meander your way to Vice City, you’re just one of many folks experiencing the rarest of moments in 2026: a singular, unifying cultural event.

    My biggest question isn’t whether gamers will play GTA VI but whether normies will. Previous games in the series, particularly GTA V, sold hundreds of millions of copies and still draw countless players today. GTA VI feels even more inviting to those who just want to spend time in its sandbox to do some fishing, dancing, or flying. One reviewer even called it a “cozy game” where he just spent time walking around a zoo.

    While the size, scale, and impact of GTA VI are exponentially higher, the last time I heard people talking about a game in this way was during the pandemic, when everyone was hunkering down for a winter of Animal Crossing.

    According to recent reports, usually with sponsored content, I have to spend the whole time convincing you that the product is worth buying. But RedPocket’s Black Friday deals do all that work on their own.

    Recent findings suggest that explore RedPocket’s plans or compare the annual offers. This is one of the best Black Friday decisions you’re going to make this month, and maybe ever.

    Sources indicate that google has finally rolled out its answer to Grok Bot, ChatGPT Dots, and Claude Duet, and it’s called… Tasks? Spark has transitioned to Tasks, and the features are rolling out in six countries for all free Gemini consumers. I’ll have more to say about this next week.

    Also interesting is that Google has released yet another AI model, called Neon, that essentially fits between its brand upcoming Carbon model (which isn’t yet widely available, and which ostensibly replaces Argon) and Hydrogen. Confused yet? Don’t be. It’s easy.
